# 

**TL;DR**\
[Prototyping.io](http://Prototyping.io) is rebuilding the design-to-manufacturing workflow from the ground up with an AI-driven approach, automating the path from CAD design to production at scale.

<https://youtu.be/q8G9q_MEzug>

**The Problem**\
Over $1T is spent annually on mechanical part manufacturing, yet the process remains largely manual.

Getting parts made still takes weeks, often with high costs and inconsistent quality. Manufacturers spend days on DFM, sourcing, programming, and setup planning before production even starts. These delays slow hardware companies down and stretch product iteration cycles.

Building locally is still expensive, largely due to fragmented operations and low machine utilization. Many companies look offshore for lower pricing, but shipping timelines, tariffs, and supply chain delays often slow product development even further.

**What We’re Building**

[Prototyping.io](http://Prototyping.io) is building autonomous manufacturing for mechanical parts by automating the workflow between CAD designs and finished parts.

The workflow today looks like:

CAD → DFM → Planning → Sourcing → Programming → Setups → Manufacturing Execution

This workflow is being rebuilt with AI-native systems and physical AI models for manufacturing.

Our approach combines AI-driven manufacturing intelligence, workflow automation, and eventually autonomous execution through industrial robotics and highly automated production systems. The goal is to dramatically reduce lead times, improve quality consistency, and enable more efficient manufacturing at scale.

**What We’re Seeing**

Demand for faster and more reliable manufacturing is growing across robotics, AI infrastructure, energy, automotive, defense, and other industries.

We’re already helping companies ranging from early-stage startups to multi-billion dollar enterprises reduce hardware iteration cycles from weeks to days by delivering high-quality parts for prototyping and early production.

**If This Resonates**

If you’re building hardware and want to move faster, we’d love to work with you.

If you’re interested in robotics, physical AI, manufacturing automation, or autonomous manufacturing and want to join the [Prototyping.io](http://Prototyping.io) team, we’d love to talk.

launches.body:
Hey everyone,

**TLDR**: we are building a new generation of UUVs (Unmanned Underwater Vehicle) for defense of critical maritime infrastructure.

The evolution of modern battlefields shows the same pattern everywhere: highly expensive military systems are increasingly being challenged by agile, low-cost technologies produced at scale.

In Ukraine, cheap aerial drones have transformed warfare and forced entire defense doctrines to adapt. We think the same shift is about to happen underwater, and are obsessed with the question of what the “drone moment” for underwater warfare would look like.

So we started speaking with submariners, naval operators, ex-commandos, and defense engineers. The demand signal was much stronger than we expected, and the common need is always the same: **cost-effective** and highly **modular** underwater **vehicles** acting in **swarms** that can **adapt quickly** to operational requirements (speed, range, sonar equipment, payloads, etc.). Today, very few solutions exist.

A couple of days after deciding to pivot, we wanted to move as fast as possible and get something real in the water before Demo Day. So we built our **first modular prototype within a week**. It already integrates the main subsystems and was designed to evolve quickly based on operator feedback and mission requirements. Here is a photo:

launches.body:
# \*\*\*\*

**TL;DR**: General Instinct distill, quantize, and deploy large frontier AI onto limited hardware on drones, old PCs, and robots.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101508&key=user_uploads/2022270/81b34033-67b0-41d9-9f7a-563ed2884da3)

**Problem**:

Physical AI (robots, drones, IoT) teams can now get frontier models to do impressive things in the lab. The hard part is getting those models to work reliably in production.

Some common patterns:

1\. Models works well in the cloud, but fails on edge in production.

2\. Custom use-cases like robots operating in the wild or in space requires on device inference.

3\. Using Gemini for everything is simply too expensive.

We built a custom, no code pipeline to solve this problem.

**What we’re building:**

Our first product: **Instinct Edge**. Give us a model, a target device, and a latency budget. We return an offline runtime that hits the budget on hardware like Jetson, mobile NPUs, ARM CPUs, Apple Neural Engine, and Snapdragons.

Under the hood, this combines compression recipes, custom CUDA / Metal / ARM NEON kernels, and a continuous data-to-serving pipeline.

One production example: a multimodal classifier on Jetson Orin NX with 111 ms cold start, 100% of decisions inside a 150 ms budget, and zero cloud calls.

**How you can help**:

If you or anyone you know are running large vision models on edge and are having problems fitting them onto your hardware, let us know by emailing [founders@general-instinct.com](mailto:founders@general-instinct.com)!

launches.title: Aseon Labs: robotic pitstops for self-driving cars
launches.tagline: A depot in-a-box for charging, cleaning & inspecting autonomous fleets
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Autonomous vehicles still rely on centralized, human-operated depots for daily charging, cleaning and servicing. Aseon builds robotic pitstops that let AV fleets reset directly inside the city, reducing downtime, dead miles and operating cost.

<https://youtu.be/4lFZU9pY1gM>

## **❌ The problem**

Autonomous driving is working. The operational layer around it is not.

Today, autonomous vehicles regularly leave high-demand zones up to 3 times per day just to charge, clean and get inspected.

Most fleets still rely on large, remote, human-operated centralized depots.

That means:

* 10–15 mile roundtrips just to reset vehicles
* vehicles out of operation for hours
* up to 44% of vehicle time spent driving empty
* as many as 1 in 3 vehicles unavailable during peak demand
* reset costs that can exceed $100 per cycle

For autonomous fleets, uptime is revenue. But today’s operating model still looks like traditional depot logistics.

## **✅ What we built**

We believe autonomous vehicles need autonomous operations, always available and distributed across the centre of the city.

So we built the Aseon pod: **a robotic pitstop station that bundles high-frequency depot workflows into a compact, rapidly deployable pod.**

Aseon Pods allow fleets to:

* charge vehicles near demand
* automatically clean interiors & exteriors
* run inspection workflows between rides
* access a reset within max. 2 miles of a vehicle’s location

Compared to traditional depot operations, Aseon can:

* reduce reset cost by up to 50%
* reduce time out of service by up to 65%
* increase revenue per vehicle by $50k+ per year

Aseon Labs is building a new category of infrastructure for autonomous fleets: robotic pitstops deployed directly where vehicles operate.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101210&key=user_uploads/180428/dacbddc1-d989-4d47-94b1-37c323826394)

## **🧩 Why us**

We’re second-time founders, building together for the second time.

Our previous company, Pushme, became the world’s largest battery-swap network for shared e-scooters and e-bikes, across 5,000 locations in 40 cities before being acquired by TIER-Dott ($600M raised).

Before Aseon:

**George Kalligeros** led TIER’s 100-person hardware organization and deployed $300M+ in fleet hardware as VP Hardware; was a mechanical engineer at Tesla.

**Dan Keene** scaled TIER energy network to 5k locations. He later served as CBO at Superduper ($4B infra). Prior to that he led 20 markets at Deliveroo (DoorDash) and worked in M&A.

If you know exceptional engineers working on robotics, autonomy, computer vision, hardware systems or industrial automation, we’d love an introduction.

Major labor shortages and the high cost of traditional automation make manufacturers and logistics companies hard and costly to operate efficiently. The world is facing a massive shortage of manual labour. It is hard to recruit and retain workers for factories and warehouses and even harder to scale. We are building robots that can be deployed instantly and work out of the box without any interruption in operations. They are semi-humanoid, which means they can fill positions designed for humans and can reliably perform any task which would take you less than 5-mins to explain to a new worker.

launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋

We're [Assil](https://www.linkedin.com/in/aahalimi/) and [Drew](https://www.linkedin.com/in/drewwalkerrr/) — co-founders of [Apollo Atomics](https://www.apolloatomics.com).

### TL;DR

Apollo Atomics took the pressurized water reactor technology that already powers 80% of the world's nuclear plants and flipped one part, the steam generator, to make the plant an order of magnitude smaller without compromising power. That single change turns a decade-long construction project into a factory-built machine that fits on a truck. We've built a working demonstrator, tested it, and our fuel is already critical before July 4th.

We put the whole story into just over two minutes — it's the clearest version of what we're building we've made so far: ▶️ <https://youtu.be/vy8y_t1KAK4?si=FmGF4Q7w6eFkn4No>

### The Problem

The existing nuclear playbook doesn't work for customers who need power now.

* Gigawatt-scale nuclear takes 10+ years and \~$20B per plant.
* Most Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) in development rely on exotic fuels, unproven coolants, or supply chains that don't exist yet.
* Customers who need power in 2030 are being told to wait until 2035+ and hope.

Data centers, industrials, and utilities have demand today — and no credible nuclear option that can ship on their timeline.

### Our Solution

Apollo builds compact pressurized water reactors — the same technology that runs \~80% of the world's nuclear plants today. The difference is that our reactor is roughly 40x more compact, because we shrank only one component: the steam generator.

We keep everything the NRC has already licensed dozens of times — light water, low-enriched uranium, fuel, and components from existing qualified supply chains. The innovation is a single part: the steam generator.

Our Compact Steam Generator (CSG) replaces the massive, hand-built steam generator at the heart of a conventional PWR with a component 20x smaller, delivering the same thermal power — pre-tested, transportable, and contracted at a fixed price. That one change is what takes a reactor from a decade-long construction project to a factory-built machine deployable in less than 24 months.

Our product roadmap is three reactors, each on a truck, each for a different customer segment:

* A-10 — 10 MWe
* A-50 — 50 MWe
* A-300 — 300 MWe

### Our Ask

If any of these are you, we'd love to talk:

* Data center operators and hyperscalers sourcing 24/7 firm power for 2028–2035 deployment.
* Industrial offtakers (chemicals, refining, heavy manufacturing) needing process heat or behind-the-meter electricity.
* Utilities evaluating SMRs for grid-connected generation.

👉 Reach us at [ahalimi@apolloatomics.com](mailto:ahalimi@apolloatomics.com) and [drew@apolloatomics.com](mailto:drew@apolloatomics.com).

Robots aren't perfect- they make mistakes and get stuck in edge cases. That means lost time, and on a factory floor or inside a logistics warehouse, that can translate to thousands of lost dollars. Keeping on-site staff on standby just to babysit them kills ROI and the deployment.

**What’s the solution?**

Our product, Sentinel, allows operators to remotely teleop their robots so they can intervene and keep robots running at 100% uptime. Our software is ultra low-latency, meaning operators can react to the environment in near real-time.

With Sentinel, robotics companies can unlock the path to scaling their deployments.

**TLDR;** Avea builds ultra low-latency teleop software that allows robotics companies to remotely control their robots using VR headsets.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101616&key=user_uploads/2215628/66a8757b-ba8a-4a6c-b573-688aba5ad815)

**What’s the problem?**

When autonomous robots get stuck during deployment, teleoperation is used to recover them and capture that edge case. Today, that means keeping on-site staff on standby just to babysit deployments. It’s not scalable and hurts ROI, causing deployments to stall.

Other remote teleop softwares are clunky and unreliable for real-time control.

**What’s the solution?**

Sentinel allows operators to remotely teleop their robots so they can intervene when autonomy breaks down. Our software has ultra low-latency, meaning operators can react to the environment in near real-time. 

With Sentinel, robotics companies can unlock the path to scaling their deployments.

**Demo Video: [https://youtu.be/dKEbWlZocJQ](https://youtu.be/dKEbWlZocJQ)**

**A bit about us:**

* We moved to SF right after graduating from UIUC last year to work on Avea
* We’ve been doing robotics since high school (shoutout FIRST!)
* We're on a mission to get robots out of the lab and into the real world

**Asks:** We want to talk to more robotics companies! If you or someone you know is an operator at a robotics company, please reach out.

name: Arlo Industries
long_description:
Arlo Industries is building a network of sensors that precisely tracks stealthy drones and aerial threats better than radars.

This capability does not exist yet because traditional radars are built on past war doctrines designed to protect single, centralised assets. Modern warfare, however, demands wide-area, persistent coverage that is both passive and economically scalable. By utilising a mesh architecture, Arlo Industries unlocks unprecedented asymmetric economics. The network is fundamentally built to scale: the cost of adding sensors grows linearly, but the tracking accuracy increases exponentially, delivering highly resilient, persistent coverage for a fraction of the cost of legacy systems.

Deo founded Arlo Industries after spending over 6 years in the Israeli defence ecosystem, where he lived through multiple conflicts and experienced the Iron Dome and other systems in action against ICBMs and the infamous Shahed drones. Learning exactly how these defence systems could be improved after a Shahed exploded close to his apartment, he built Arlo Industries around the core philosophy that conflict should be concise & precise.

The people behind Arlo1 includes a PhD in drones and autonomy and military experts.

Arlo Industries has actively showcased this technology directly to Ukrainian militaries on the frontlines, as well as to operators across Europe and the USA.

launches.tagline: We build sensors that track drones & missiles better than radars
launches.body:
---

**Hi, I'm Deo, founder of [Arlo Industries](https://arlo1.com/).**

<https://youtu.be/2F0cugbrq3A>

**The problem**

Modern air defence depends on active radars: expensive, emitting, and targetable. A single ground-based radar unit can cost tens of millions, broadcasts its location to anything listening, and leaves massive coverage gaps against low-altitude threats like drones.

This architecture was built for a different era. Today's threat, swarms of cheap drones and cruise missiles flying below radar coverage, exploits every weakness of centralised, active sensing.

**What we're building**

Mentat is a passive, distributed sensing network.

* **Tracks aerial objects in 3D without emitting**: invisible to the threats it detects
* **Accurately track smaller threats**: our mesh works together to better pinpoint small targets
* **Scales via many low-cost nodes**: instead of a few high-value targets, we employ asymmetric economics where adding nodes grows linearly in cost but tracking accuracy increases exponentially

We're the sensing layer, the force multiplier for every interceptor and C-UAS system in the market.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101954&key=user_uploads/836806/ddbe92c9-897d-4e52-90ab-c8574ed7335c)

**What we're really building**

Drone detection is our wedge, not our ceiling. The real innovation isn't in any single sensor, it's in the network that ties it all together. We're building the foundational sensing and communications infrastructure layer for frontline defence. A distributed, resilient network that future defence technologies will plug into. Like the **Starlink before the Starship.**

**Why now**

Low-altitude airspace is increasingly contested. Ukraine, Nordics, Eastern Europe, & Middle East, operators everywhere are discovering that the cost curve of traditional radar doesn't scale against distributed drone threats. At the same time, edge compute, distributed systems, and passive optical sensing have reached the point where a fundamentally different architecture is viable.

**Backstory**

I spent 6+ years in Israel, living through multiple conflicts and seeing systems like Iron Dome operate against ballistic missiles and drones firsthand. When a Shahed drone exploded near my apartment, the gap between what exists and what's needed became personal. Since then, I've been in Ukraine and across Eastern Europe, working directly with military operators and validating in real conflict environments.

📍Field Test - Ukraine

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101954&key=user_uploads/836806/b380d961-dde4-4e50-b6eb-1cbf708e6d3c)

**Traction**

* Active technology demonstrations with Ukrainian military on the frontlines
* Partnerships and military relationships across USA, Ukraine, Finland, and Estonia.
* Team includes a PhD in drones/autonomy and military domain experts

**Our asks**

🔧 **Hiring:** We're looking for engineers in optics, signal processing, long-range comms, mesh networks, and off-grid embedded systems → [Jobs page](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/arlo-industries/jobs)

🤝 **Intros:** Defense operators, C-UAS companies, or critical infrastructure partners (airports, energy, borders) dealing with aerial awareness gaps → please reach out on [Linkedin](https://www.linkedin.com/in/deoarlo/)

launches.title: Maquoketa Research: Guidance systems for one-way attack drones
launches.tagline: The drone intelligence layer
launches.body:
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uI5-M8w8UEs>

**More than 70% of combat casualties now come from drones.** They have proven to be the most cost-effective tool of modern warfare, and the Department of War plans to buy over 1 million of them in the next 2-3 years. So what’s the problem? **Less than 25% of drones successfully strike their target.** 

It takes months to years of training for military operators to perfect the flight maneuvers needed to use FPV drones effectively. And even highly skilled operators remain vulnerable to electronic warfare, GPS denial, and adverse weather conditions.

But what if it wasn’t so hard? What if someone who had never flown a drone before could pick one up and hit a moving target with expert-level accuracy, even under jammed conditions?

**Our Solution:**

We build platform-agnostic terminal guidance modules for one-way attack drones. Our guidance system has been shown to increase successful strike rates from under 25% to **upwards of 80%**. At the core of the system is a custom object tracking algorithm that maintains target lock under adverse conditions and can re-acquire a target lock even after 5 seconds of target occlusion, all while running on hardware costing under $200. Because inference happens onboard, the drone can continue tracking and engaging targets even after link degradation or jamming.

Current approaches usually fall into two categories. The first approach is to make bespoke drones that include custom target detection and terminal guidance systems, but these drones cost upwards of $40k a unit. Existing modular compute solutions that allow for running target tracking models and terminal guidance algorithms can require a complete redesign of the drone, often don’t have their own dedicated camera or radio, and typically cost nearly the same price as the drone itself.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102393&key=user_uploads/2184565/c1cd3c2e-ddb1-4287-85ba-0407ff915ab1)

Our solution fixes the problems with both traditional approaches. Our system integrates with existing FPV drones through a single connection to the flight controller. Because it includes its own camera, compute, and radio stack, it operates independently of the drone’s native avionics and communications systems. And because the compute is so cheap, autonomous terminal guidance becomes economically viable even for disposable FPV platforms. 

By standardizing compute, sensing, and communications across heterogeneous drone platforms, we also are creating a foundation for swarm operations, large scale coordination, and data aggregation.

**The Team:**

Three of us (Dave, Aidan, Evan) met through high school robotics five years ago. We became close after starting our first project, an electromagnetic railgun. Before the project got shut down by the FBI, it was the most powerful such device ever built by a hobbyist. Evan started programming at age 8 and later completed Berkeley’s EECS program in just 5 semesters, where he met Alex. Alex entered Berkeley at 16 and researched state-of-the-art sub-THz phased array systems. Aidan started building liquid fueled rocket engines when he was 15. Dave studied computer science at UIC before dropping out after he built the fastest growing game on Roblox, which has since generated over $45M in revenue.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102393&key=user_uploads/2184565/74758a28-ded7-45a9-b85e-44be11fc8eda)

**The Ask:**

We’re looking for introductions to drone manufacturers, defense primes, and government programs exploring low-cost autonomous terminal guidance and interoperability across heterogeneous drone platforms.

launches.title: Proprio Robotics - Autonomous Data Centers

launches.body:
![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106864&key=user_uploads/2910355/e9094f01-f5e9-4c30-93c6-81d8f041957d)

### **Physical AI for Data Centers**

Over the next five years, more than $7 trillion is projected to flow into data center buildout. But the supply chain is still heavily manual and fragmented, and can’t keep pace with current demand. **Proprio Robotics** is building autonomous robots for the entire data center lifecycle—assembly, maintenance, and decommissioning.

See our [launch video!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=999uFeKGyVY)

### **The Problem**

Building and running AI compute infrastructure requires dealing with delicate and fragile components that traditional automation simply cannot do. As a result, servers are manually assembled by hand overseas, and spend weeks in transit before they are integrated into racks and delivered to data centers. Once they get there, labor constraints exacerbate the issue of maintenance. Today, hundreds of thousands of technician positions go unfilled in the United States. Finally, when the servers are retired, there is no efficient way to extract valuable components inside like GPUs and memory.

### **What We're Building**

We develop physical AI models and custom hardware, purpose-made to give robots the dexterity and intelligence to perform various server-related manipulation tasks.

* **Assembly** **-** Autonomous robots can assemble servers onshore without driving up labor costs, supporting the growing need to bring ODMs back to the United States.
* **Maintenance** **-** We use the same technology for live data center maintenance. We built a working AI data center in our office, and our robot can actively maintain it 24/7. We’re deploying this technology to commercial data centers in the coming months.
* **Decommissioning** **-** Our robots also break down previous-generation servers and pull out reusable parts, and we're working with enterprise circular programs and IT Asset Disposition companies to return scarce components to circulation.

### **Why This Matters**

The immense demand for compute requires new innovation. 

To solve power and cooling constraints, operators are building data centers away from the grid, near nuclear facilities, on the water, and in space—environments where it’s not easy to staff humans. With autonomous data centers, we can take human ergonomics and labor constraints out of the picture and redesign entire facilities from scratch.                    

### **Who We Are**

We're graduate robotics researchers out of **Berkeley AI Research** and **Harvard AI and Robotics Lab**. Anirudh’s spent years working at one of the country's leading robotics labs, training dexterous manipulation models alongside NVIDIA's GR00T team. Raghav’s led research centered on reinforcement learning and humanoid world models. Both of us are extremely excited to bring this expertise to the AI compute industry, where robotic automation will be indispensable for meeting demand.

### **Our Ask**

As we advance our technology, we’d like to push for more commercial deployments. If you / anybody you know works in any stage of the AI compute lifecycle, we’d love to chat. Reach out to us at [founders@propriorobotics.com](mailto:founders@propriorobotics.com) :)

launches.title: Edgerun: The 10 lb Military Exoskeleton
launches.tagline: Powered exoskeleton that assists every step a soldier takes under combat load
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Edgerun builds powered legs for soldiers. A 10 lb exoskeleton worn at the waist that adds assistance to every step and cuts the effort of moving under a combat load by 30-45%. Since May, we've run 100+ field tests with Ukrainian operators out of our Kyiv field office.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nFLeQV2DWMc>

**▍The problem**

Every system on the modern battlefield has been upgraded. The human carrying it has not.

* For 2,500 years the soldier's load sat around 40 lbs. In the last 40 years it **doubled, then doubled again**.
* A US infantryman now carries **90-140 lbs** into a fight. The Army's own field manual sets the limit at 48 lbs.
* On deployment, load carriage causes **twice as many** evacuations as enemy contact.
* The Pentagon and VA spend **$9.3B a year** on the injuries it leaves behind.

Battles are won through speed and surprise. Load kills both.

**▍Why now**

Sixty years of military exoskeletons died the same death. The device cost more to carry than it gave back. SOCOM's TALOS burned $400M before it was cancelled in 2019.

That all changed in the last 18 months. The humanoid robotics boom produced one-pound actuators that put out 30+ Nm of torque, and 21700 cells crossed 450 Wh/kg. The components finally exist. They’re getting better every quarter.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112214&key=user_uploads/1393855/cd255b24-3429-4270-9670-e28fc8df360b)

**▍What we built**

Our first exoskeleton is a bilateral hip system worn at the waist. It reads your gait in real time and adds torque at the moment your hip drives forward. The hip produces about 60% of the force in loaded walking, so assisting it gives the most help-per-pound of anything you could strap to the body.

* Under 10 lbs with batteries
* 30-45% less metabolic cost under a combat load
* On in 5 seconds, off in one
* 12+ hours on hot-swappable drone-class batteries
* Quasi-direct-drive actuators, composite structures, CAN bus. Nothing exotic by design.

The soldier arrives at the objective still able to fight, patrols 10 km farther, and keeps a body that lasts past one tour.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112214&key=user_uploads/1393855/94bf48a9-0ba6-4ce7-94a2-f467cae9657c)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112214&key=user_uploads/1393855/883d1e98-900a-420a-b7ff-e56cc8911c0c)

**▍Ukraine**

Our field engineers work out of a Kyiv office, alongside operators from infantry, special operations, and National Guard units who provide structured feedback every day. [Balistyka](https://balistyka.ua/), one of Ukraine's leading body armor makers, is an integration partner, helping us ensure our system fits the kit soldiers already wear.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112214&key=user_uploads/1393855/89a30d39-fe11-421c-abe7-32961da8d1bd)

**▍The mission**

Defense is the first customer, not the last. Read the mission at edgerun.com/mission

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
American manufacturers lose an estimated $285,000 annually to poor quality for every $10 million in revenue. At the same time, the industry is losing the engineers who know how to prevent those losses. Nearly 4 million manufacturing jobs will need to be filled by 2033 as experienced workers retire, and almost half are expected to go unfilled. Much of the expertise required to review complex engineering drawings exists only in the heads of senior engineers who are leaving the workforce.

We're both engineers who grew up watching this firsthand. After more than 200 conversations with manufacturing engineers, quality engineers and machinists, we're building software that captures that expertise by automatically reviewing engineering drawings against ASME standards and company-specific rules before they ever reach the shop floor.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
We're building the largest repository of engineering judgment in the world. We tailor each company's checks to their own standards, the kind usually mastered by only a handful of senior engineers. We turn that knowledge into software every plant can use the same week.

With success, the physical things the world depends on get built 10x faster, and a retiring generation's expertise is never lost.

launches.title: HERA: catches thousand-dollar drawing mistakes before the shop floor.
launches.tagline: Hera reviews every drawing against your factory's own standards and the ASME code, catching expensive mistakes and preventing rework 10x faster than manual review.
launches.body:
**TL;DR: Every custom metal part starts as a drawing, and every drawing gets checked by hand before anyone builds it. Hera does that check in minutes instead of a full day, and catches the mistakes that turn into scrapped parts.**

[**https://youtu.be/J_5NRjkou3Y**](https://youtu.be/J_5NRjkou3Y)

**The Problem**

Custom mechanical parts run on 2D drawings. Whether you're an OEM releasing drawings to suppliers, or an aerospace supplier answering to source inspection, every drawing has to be checked against ASME/ISO standards and GD&T requirements before it goes anywhere near a machine.

Right now, that review is done by hand, and usually by the most senior engineer in the building. And a single missed tolerance callout or an ambiguous datum reference can mean a scrapped part, a blown schedule, or a shipment that fails inspection.

We heard the same story from a pressure vessel fabricator, a semiconductor tooling shop, and a medical device manufacturer: reviews take days. This isn't because the work is hard. There's simply no good way to do it faster without cutting corners, and nobody cuts corners on a drawing that could scrap a $40,000 part.

**Our Solution**

Hera is a brain for manufacturing. Any real advance in manufacturing has to be grounded in two things: the standards parts are held to and the reality of the shop floor. So that's what we built Hera on.

Upload a drawing and Hera checks GD&T callouts, tolerance stack ups, and title block requirements against ASME Y14.5, relevant ISO standards, and your own design intent. The result is a drawing your shop can build right the first time, without the delays and rework that eat margins. Every review also makes Hera more valuable, creating a system of record for drawing errors that helps teams build better models for engineering processes.

**While the current review takes days, Hera takes minutes… and gets better by the drawing.**

**Us**

**Noelle** grew up in an industrial park her family runs in the Philippines and has been on factory floors her whole life. At 19, she built a water-treatment facility that added 40 L/s of capacity to the park. 

**Meera** has spent years around manufacturing: at her family's plants, and on projects at Pfizer and TE Connectivity, where she built a SOTA discrete-event simulation. She taught herself PLC programming and C++, and has published ML research at UW.

We actually met on a bus to a factory tour, and have been best friends ever since!

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107030&key=user_uploads/3352287/d05e9e1a-57c8-4e43-91d7-75e42a004261)

**Our Ask** If you run or work at a factory (aerospace, semiconductor, medical device, pressure vessel, or custom machinery), we want to visit you! If you invite us out to see your shop, we’ll come by in person and bring you a **customized Hera Swiss Army knife**.

Reach out to us at [**founders@manufacturingintelligence.org**](mailto:founders@manufacturingintelligence.org).

🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110611&key=user_uploads/3652354/be41c9e5-378d-452f-a111-10380035f14d)

**Every electric motor runs on rare-earth magnets.** EVs, drones, robots, wind turbines, guided munitions: nearly all of them are dependent on Chinese magnets. On January 1st, 20270, [regulation changes will make it illegal to deliver anything that walks, drives, or flies to US Defense if it contains a magnet produced in covered countries like China.](https://www.massmagnetics.com/comply) The domestic supply chain meant to replace it doesn't exist yet. **Mines take a decade to permit, and the ore they pull up leaves radioactive tailings behind, making permitting magnet mining a nightmare.**

We’re[ ](https://www.linkedin.com/in/energyeric)the founders, [Eric Silver](https://x.com/metalscontent) and [Matthew Grol](https://www.linkedin.com/in/matthew-groll/)l (left and right in the pic below). We’ve known each other since grade school. Since then, Eric’s built multiple battery pilot production lines and materials science labs in the Midwest for NSF-funded companies. Matthew’s built exquisite aerospace gear including Moon-regolith melters and ultra-precise guidance systems for the world’s foremost labs at NASA, Draper, and MIT. **Together we’re making one bet: America's rare-earth problem isn't a mining problem.**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110611&key=user_uploads/3652354/2046e9de-2db6-47e8-91fc-651e31e5a834)

**Mass Magnetics’ unfair advantage is sitting in end-of-life electric vehicles, hard drives, and industrial equipment.** The team uses AI models and robotics trained on real scrap to sort metallurgy by exact grade and chemistry. Then, a rapid-sintering process takes that reclaimed mass to a finished magnet in 3 minutes, where conventional approaches take over 4 hours. The result is a magnet as strong as anything imported, with no radioactive footprint or bureaucratic permitting, fully compliant for US defense.

**If you build robots, drones or motors visit our site and reach out at [outreach@massmagnetics.com](mailto:outreach@massmagnetics.com) and get your magnets.**

launches.tagline: Kara grows and engineers diamond wafers for thermal management, semiconductor and quantum applications
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** We grow high-purity diamond wafers for scientific and industrial applications. Our diamond thermal wafers can be used in aircraft, spacecraft, RF electronics, and lasers to move heat dramatically better than conventional materials. We’re helping hardware run cooler, faster, and more reliably with diamond that is 5× more thermally conductive than copper.

Here is a link to our launch video: 

<https://youtu.be/16aad1cU_FM>

**The Problem**

The world’s most valuable hardware systems are limited by how quickly they can remove heat.

For AI chips, that means expensive GPUs throttle and deliver less compute. In aircraft and satellites, it means carrying more cooling mass. In RF systems and lasers, it limits sustained output power.

Adding more cooling costs space, and energy, and sometimes is simply not possible.

**What We Built**

Diamond is usually something you wear. We make it something engineers can build with.

Diamond conducts heat up to **5× better than copper while weighing \~60% less** for the same volume. It is electrically insulating and stable in extreme environments.

Today we manufacture:

* Diamond heat spreaders for AI and high-performance computing
* Ultra-high-purity diamond wafers for thermal, photonic and quantum applications
* Diamond-metal composites (copper and aluminium) for thermal management
* Metallized and bondable diamond plates
* Custom-engineered diamond components

We are now producing custom samples under pilot agreements and purchase orders for thermal, electronic, aerospace, and quantum applications.

Silicon transformed computing when we learned to manufacture it with extreme purity and control. Kara is doing the same with diamond. Today, our ultra-high-purity diamond pulls heat away from silicon chips.

**Tomorrow, Kara’s control over purity and defects unlocks diamond as the ultimate semiconductor.**

**Why us**

[@Aarin Jhaveri](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/3669602) is a fifth-generation diamantaire who has sold millions of dollars in natural and lab-grown diamonds and worked across the supply chain.

[@Anuveer Chadha](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/3669310) is a chemical engineer who has worked on diamond quantum sensing and advanced-materials research at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory with the Department of Defense and Department of Energy.

Diamond is our unfair advantage. We know how to grow, control, and engineer it far beyond jewelry.

**Our ask**

**Today, we're looking for introductions to engineers building hardware that is limited by heat.** 

Specifically:

* AI accelerator packaging teams
* Advanced packaging / OSAT engineers
* Aerospace, space, and defence electronics
* Data-centre infrastructure companies
* High-power RF and GaN teams

Introduce us to the engineer responsible for the hottest, hardest-to-cool hardware, especially where size, weight, or power makes cooling difficult. 

We’ll build them a custom diamond sample to test.

Email us at [founders@karalabs.ai](mailto:founders@karalabs.ai) or book time here: <https://calendly.com/aarin-berkeley/aarin-jhaveri-s-calender>

**Diamond spent centuries as a symbol of “extraordinary”. We are making it something the world can build with.**

launches.title: Enact: post-training infrastructure for robotics models
launches.tagline: Enact generates the data and evaluations needed to make robotics models reliable in the real world.
launches.body:
**TL;DR: Enact helps teams deploy robots that work in the real world. We roll out policies, generate failure / recovery data, and run in-house evaluations so robots can complete real tasks in production.** 

[**https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dam0tQBIezY**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dam0tQBIezY)

**The Problem**

Robotics models can look flawless in choreographed demos and still fail when an object slips, the scene shifts, or the robot makes an early mistake. Those failures push the policy into states its training data never taught it to recover from. **Robotics models must train on edge cases to be reliable in the real world.**

**What We Built**

Enact turns a policy’s failures into targeted recovery datasets for teams training robotics models. We use the data to fine-tune models and run real-world evaluations, verifying our data improves reliability.

**We’re already serving our first customers: finding where their robots fail and collecting the targeted recovery data needed to make them robust.**

* Roll out an existing model on a physical robot.
* Identify recurring failure states.
* Recreate those states and demonstrate how to recover.
* Retrain with the new trajectories added in.
* Repeat

**Targeted recovery data pushes success rates above 99%.**

On our controlled packing task using pi0.5 on the YAM 6DoF arms:

* 200 ordinary expert demonstrations: 90/100 successful physical rollouts
* 250 ordinary expert demonstrations (more of the same data): 89/100
* 200 expert demonstrations plus 50 targeted recovery demonstrations: 99/100

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109880&key=user_uploads/2406199/e1b83c19-6e1d-4dda-adcf-258398bc1676)

**We’re continuing to longer-horizon tasks such as industrial kitting, lab automation, and electronics recycling**

Longer-horizon tasks need substantially more base and recovery data, but the loop is the same: find failures, target missing behaviors, retrain, repeat.

**Who We Are**

We’re James Stevens and Govind Chada, and we met at Stanford. Govind researched real-world robot adaptation in Chelsea Finn’s IRIS Lab and co-developed recovery methods published at top robotics conferences. Together, we built Enact’s in-house data and evaluation operation and are already serving robotics teams. We started Enact to make robotics models work reliably outside the lab.

**Our Ask**

Training a robot foundation model or deploying a policy that fails on a real task? Tell us the model, task, and where it breaks, and we’ll make it work.

Email: [founders@enact.company](mailto:founders@enact.company)

launches.tagline: Semiconductors to push machines where humans cant go.
launches.body:
<https://youtu.be/oHKXAeiH79Y>

**TLDR:** Synapse Semiconductor builds image sensors that process **AI on the sensor** itself. Each pixel captures light and runs neural-network computation in the same device, replacing the need for a GPU while cutting the power and latency of edge vision.\
\
\
A camera has no use by itself. Its value is only when its information gets evaluated. How can a camera that only has value when combined with a GPU support local intelligence? GPUs will get better, yet the fundamental problem is the separation of the camera and the GPU. Solving that separation will unlock bountiful innovation in machine perception. 

**RETINA: a chip designed like the human retina which runs neural network operations in the camera pixel.** 

\
We have compressed the whole edge AI vision hardware stack into **one wafer**. CNNS, VLMS, etc can run on just one chip that senses light. Our compute transistors are also the same photosensors that see light. There is no longer separation between compute (Nvidia Jetson Nano) and a camera (RealSense Depth Camera). \
\
If you are building robotic perception, drones, and vision systems for physical AI —> [book.synapsesemi.org](http://book.synapsesemi.org)

launches.body:
# 

We build containerized cells of autonomous interceptors that protect critical civilian infrastructure from hostile drones. Park the cell next to anything you need to keep running: it detects an incoming threat, launches and physically neutralizes the incoming aerial threat. [www.impact-drones.com](http://www.impact-drones.com)

**OUR LAUNCH VIDEO**

<https://youtu.be/qLqx0dcpcGo>

**TL;DR:** Half this batch is building AI agents. Your agents live in data centers. And these sites are now under threat. In March, drones took three AWS data centers offline in the Middle East and a dozen core cloud services with them. **Amazon lost 200 million USD in one day.** We sell a box you put next to anything you'd rather keep: an interceptor pierces its own lid, and the threat stops existing. We'll keep your agents running.

**Why now:** The drone threat went industrial and air defense math didn't.

**A single patriot missile costs more than 1m USD to shoot down a drone worth 30k USD.** Critical infrastructure needs a defense system that can be deployed at scale without losing the cost-per-interception battle.

**What we're building:** a cell holding autonomous interceptors, always charged, always ready for when a threat arises. Unlike jamming, our system physically intercepts the threat. Unlike conventional air-defense systems, it is designed specifically for protecting civilian infrastructure affordably and at scale.

**Why us:** two founders who ship hardware fast.

[@Jasper Lortije](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/3245067): aerospace engineer (MSc at TU Delft), previously founded a Dutch company building GNSS-denied visual navigation for autonomous systems.

[@Alessandro Fiume](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/3677968): sales and operations, ex Bloomberg, MSBA at Columbia.

**Our ask:** intros to the people who own the airspace problem: data center security and infrastructure leads (hyperscalers and neoclouds especially, your uptime now has an air defense dependency), airport operations directors, and energy grid security teams. And if you're building agents: we're literally your uptime insurance, come say hi. name: Rise Reforming
long_description:
Geopolitical conflicts and natural disasters frequently expose the vulnerability of the American chemical industry. The reason? Production is centralized and fossil fuel-dependent. The solution? Localized production using an undervalued resource: biogas. The US produces enough biogas to make over $20 bn/y worth of chemicals, but 60% is wasted in low-margin applications or flared altogether.

Rise Reforming is commercializing a modular process to transform this underutilized biogas on-site into cheap, supply-secure chemicals. Our beachhead market is dimethyl ether (DME), used as an aerosol propellant and a low-carbon fuel additive in propane. Our target market is methanol: an established billion $ chemical and the future of low-carbon shipping.

We're doing our pilot project at a Chicagoland wastewater plant. This will be the first wastewater biogas-to-methanol demo in the Americas.

We're hiring for a senior chemical process engineer. Apply here: https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/rise-reforming/jobs/wJ9Q9nv-senior-chemical-process-engineer

launches.title: GUILD - New Generation of Defense Contractor
launches.tagline: Making aerospace and naval parts faster and cheaper for defense
launches.body:
Hey everyone 🙂 - we’re [@Kaya Celebi](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/3161464) and [@Erim Gurlemis](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/3163115) , co-founders of [@GUILD](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/32194) .

**TL;DR**

[@GUILD](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/32194) **is an AI-native defense contractor making aerospace parts faster and cheaper than today’s supply chain**. We win government contracts, turn technical requirements into production-ready workflows, and execute through factory integrations that eliminate the weeks normally lost between RFQ and factory floor. <https://guildai.co>

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109739&key=user_uploads/3161464/3cf82073-c0e0-4c42-8d2b-d4fab3e159ca)

We’re building GUILD in two connected motions:

* First, we win and execute government manufacturing contracts directly.
* Second, we help defense hardware companies turn designs, technical packages, and supply-chain requirements into executable procurement and production workflows.

In both cases, the goal is the same: move from technical requirements to manufactured parts faster, with less cost and less operational drag.

**THE PROBLEM**

Government contracting is fragmented, overcomplicated, and inaccessible. That makes defense manufacturing slower and more expensive than it should be.

The government waits too long and pays too much for parts the country already knows how to make. Meanwhile, the supplier base is shrinking: DoW’s reported in 2023 that small-business participation in the defense industrial base has fallen by over 40% in the last decade.

**Less competition means fewer options, higher prices, weaker supply chains, and more critical work stuck before it ever reaches a production floor.** 

**THE CAUSE**

The defense supply chain is not wired together. Government demand, technical requirements, manufacturer capability, financial markets, and execution data all live in different places, so every contract becomes a manual search problem - stuck in PDFs, portals, spreadsheets, and domain knowledge.

The hard part is not finding government opportunities. Anyone can have Claude build a scrape-bot for [SAM.gov](http://SAM.gov) and call it a pipeline. **The hard part is turning messy technical requirements into a manufacturing decision, then executing the work.**

This favors large incumbents who can throw teams of people at the problem. Smaller manufacturers usually cannot. They either spend weeks decoding the package, price in too much risk, miss the timing, or never enter the market at all.

**OUR APPROACH**

**GUILD is the prime contractor**, not a marketplace or lead-gen layer for manufacturers. We win government work directly. We break the technical package into the operational steps required to produce and deliver the part. Then we execute.

**The core of this is our company brain: a structural ontology of defense manufacturing.**

AI-native, to us, means the company documents and learns from its own execution. Every artifact around a contract - requirements, quotes, supplier interactions, decisions, awards, workflows, and deliveries - becomes structured memory. Our agents traverse that graph to understand what a part is, how it can be made, what it should cost, and what needs to happen next.

The company brain compounds. Every bid makes the next bid smarter. Every factory handoff improves the next handoff. Every delivery teaches the system what actually happened, not just what the plan said. That is what lets us move from document parsing to execution as the contractor responsible for the work.

**WHAT WE’VE BUILT**

We’ve built the company brain that turns technical packages into executable manufacturing workflows. It ingests messy contract packages, understands the requirements, prices work against known factory capability, generates the production path, and keeps improving as new parts, factories, and outcomes enter the system.

This is not a hard-coded set of workflows. The system helps us build and refine new workflows as it observes more of the defense manufacturing knowledge space. GUILD Forge is the interface for this: a procurement and production planning system for defense companies that need to move from technical design to supply-chain execution.

**WHAT WE MAKE**

Our current focus is aerospace precision metals. That includes jet and engine components, structural and wing-adjacent parts, housings, brackets, fittings, retainers, and the simple but critical hardware that sits inside larger aerospace systems.

These parts are not always glamorous, but they are everywhere. When their supply chain is slow, expensive, or opaque, the larger programs above them slow down too.

**THE TEAM**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109739&key=user_uploads/3161464/9f3944e0-0a34-426b-a920-033542ce928f)

Kaya has an MS in Computer Science from Columbia and studied CS + Statistics at Duke. His background is in ML research, AI modernization, and quant work: he worked on AI modernization and quantitative systems at Morgan Stanley, and later led an AI team at hedge fund Hartree Partners. Coming into defense from the outside forced him to learn the industry from first principles and turn that learning into GUILD's technical architecture.

Erim studied Biological Sciences at Rutgers University, where he conducted research on metabolism before working in pharma consulting supporting oncology research. He then pivoted into finance at Morgan Stanley. There, he led full-scale AI implementation for Wealth Management & Advisory. At GUILD, he turns the messy reality of defense manufacturing, supplier coordination, pricing and execution into operating requirements our system can handle.

**THE ASK**

We’d love intros to defense companies that need better access to procurement, people with government or program connections, and teams dealing with supply-chain pain around technical packages, suppliers, compliance, packaging, or delivery.

We’re especially interested in meeting defense hardware companies, aerospace manufacturers, primes, and manufacturers with end-to-end automation capability - the kind of partners where GUILD can integrate directly into the factory operating layer, not just send PDFs back and forth.

Email us at [founders@guildai.co](mailto:founder@guildai.co) or visit <https://guildai.co>.

\-  Kaya + Erim 🧿

name: Exosat
long_description:
Exosat is building thousands of low-cost communication satellites to provide a neutral, sovereign alternative to Starlink. By designing our satellites with zero ITAR/EAR-controlled content, we can leverage manufacturers anywhere in the world to produce our satellites at under a tenth of the cost and launch them from other nations to bypass capacity bottlenecks and access equatorial orbits. 

We're starting off by selling connectivity to device OEMs and network operators, but will eventually use the distributed compute across our constellation to run low-latency inference for robots and autonomous vehicles in remote and rural areas anywhere on the planet.

We've already signed hundreds of millions in LOIs to work with operators across Central Asia, Southeast Asia, and the Middle East, booked our first satellite launch next year, and hold an 11,000 satellite filing with the ITU to build the largest comms network outside of the U.S. and China.
one_liner: Building a neutral, sovereign alternative to Starlink

launches.title: Exosat — Building a sovereign Starlink
launches.tagline: Building thousands of low-cost communication satellites as a neutral, sovereign alternative to Starlink. We launch the first one next April.
launches.body:
**TL;DR: Exosat is building a sovereign alternative to Starlink with thousands of low-cost satellites. We’ve booked our first launch next April and signed hundreds of millions in LOIs with customers across six nations. We’re looking to connect with operators interested in sovereign networks and AI infrastructure. Email us: [founders@exosat.com](mailto:founders@exosat.com)**

Exosat is building thousands of low-cost communication satellites to provide a neutral, sovereign alternative to Starlink. 

We launch our first satellite **next April**, have signed **$400M in LOIs** with customers across 6 nations, and hold an ITU filing for 11,000 satellites to build the largest comms network outside of the United States and China.

[Video](https://youtu.be/aABRZfcYAFQ)

### **⏰ Problem**

Nations and enterprises are wary about depending on Starlink.

These concerns aren’t without merit. In 2022, Starlink access was suddenly cut to stop a Ukrainian counteroffensive. As a result, nations have realized that a foreign superpower owning your satellites makes you ultimately dependent on their continued permission to access it.

In Europe, telecoms are warning about the danger of relying on foreign-owned AI and satellite infrastructure:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109889&key=user_uploads/689300/9dc3272a-bf85-4710-ad4d-e4592100ca1e)

In Indonesia, telecoms are lobbying for a Starlink ban:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109889&key=user_uploads/689300/5596ba12-4d01-4acd-b11c-8b1e777bb663)

In India, Starlink rollout has been delayed due to security concerns:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109889&key=user_uploads/689300/e4e7cd9a-e67d-42f8-bd8a-c1a78a0f4034)

And even nations like Canada are moving off of dependence on American space infrastructure:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109889&key=user_uploads/689300/b73fbed9-3742-4105-8a86-de42843dbd1b)

But even if they don’t trust Starlink, that doesn’t mean they necessarily trust constellations like Qianfan or Guowang that are owned and operated by Chinese state enterprises.

However, other alternatives outside of the U.S. and China face years of delay or need millions of dollars just to build a single satellite, which leaves hundreds of millions people still without reliable connectivity. 

### **🛰️ Our Solution**

Exosat fixes this problem by building thousands of satellites at a tenth of the usual cost.

We focus entirely on civil and commercial customers outside of the United States or China and fly our satellites in lower orbits versus incumbents like AST and Iridium, enabling us to take advantage of better link budgets, faster latency, and a milder radiation environment.

These factors let us use global manufacturing hubs or local partners to build our satellites using automotive-grade parts and **zero** ITAR/EAR-controlled supply chains, enabling us to seamlessly launch from other nations to bypass capacity bottlenecks and access equatorial orbits.

As a result, we can deploy a communications satellite with a 3-5 year lifespan for **\~$300k instead of $5M** and in days instead of months, enabling us to manufacture and deploy a mega-constellation at near cost-parity to Starlink.

**Our thesis is simple: we’re building a satellite at <10% of the cost to dominate 80% of the market instead of going after everyone.**

### **👋 About Us**

I’m a second-time space founder who previously built Aethero, a company developing satellite edge computers. We scaled to millions of dollars in revenue from defense primes like Blue Origin and Booz Allen Hamilton, won multiple SBIR awards, launched two satellites to orbit, and did radiation research on GPUs with the Aerospace Corporation and AFRL.

I started Exosat and moved to Singapore because I think a future where SpaceX and China monopolize the space economy is a bleak one. I’m willing to go for broke, and put down the deposit for our first launch slot next year with my own money.

### **📈 What have we done?**

Since starting out this summer, we’ve:

* **Booked our first launch** for next April, with early pilots underway to start initial commercial service for satellite IoT no later than the end of 2028.
* **Added $400M+ in LOIs** from early customers across Southeast Asia, the Middle East, and Central Asia to either lease future network capacity from our dedicated constellation or build and launch their own sovereign networks with our satellites.
* **Published ITU filings to build an 11,000 satellite constellation** to build the biggest satellite network outside of the United States and China.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109889&key=user_uploads/689300/2420ddf1-1da9-4f74-b6ef-15dd51f24eb2)

### **🙏 Our Ask**

If any of these describe you or your organization, we'd love to talk:

* Network operators interested in space-based capacity
* National space agencies interested in sovereign space capabilities
* Industrial users in maritime, energy, mining, logistics, who rely on satellites for tasks such as AIS or remote connectivity
* OEMs producing satellite-connected devices and gateways

👉 Reach us at [info@exosat.com](mailto:info@exosat.com)

**Fun fact:** We’re the first YC space company to be based in Asia.

launches.title: Agency Tool Company: The build and deployment platform for robotics
launches.tagline: Field Robots Faster with ATC Deploy
launches.body:
Today we're sharing Agency Tool Company and our first product, ATC Deploy: a faster, more reliable way to ship software to robots wherever they are. It moves updates up to 20 times faster than docker pull or scp and works with any software stack already in use.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jx0rLRVa06s>

## The updates that took until 2 a.m.

Davis and I spent eight years building Scythe Robotics and putting hundreds of autonomous mowers to work across the country. For years, we deployed software with a tool I'd cobbled together for our first few robots. As the fleet grew, deployment became an ordeal: engineers stayed up until 2 a.m., we coordinated with customers to move robots out of sheds and into LTE coverage at set times, and failed transfers restarted from zero. Shipping a fix could take more coordination than building it. We had models to train and customers to serve, so the tooling limped along with incremental bandaids.

We've since heard the same story from robotics teams across industries. That deployment becomes a hidden bottleneck: teams become release-averse, feedback loops slow and improvements stall. Stitched-together web and IoT tools barely work if you know which scripts to run and who to call, so they survive, even if it means every update is distracting from improving the product.

## What we built

ATC Deploy ships whatever you already run: OS images, Docker images, or any file tree. Run “atc ota push user@robot”, and it sends only the changed bytes, then restarts your software through hooks you define—way faster than a docker push.

Install takes one “curl | sh” command and a config file so you can get back to work fast. Interrupted transfers resume where they stopped, and an offline robot can receive updates by USB if you need. There's no new runtime, packaging format, or operating system to adopt.

## Shipping to robots today

ATC Deploy already ships software to robots at Burro, which has deployed more than 750 machines worldwide, Tempo, polishing concrete across several US states and Canada, and Gather, who is scaling their 99.9% accurate inventory drones nationwide. Their teams spend less time managing delivery and more time improving the robot.

**Operate a robot fleet? Join the ATC Deploy waitlist at [agencytool.com](https://agencytool.com/).** Know a team that should be using it? Send them this post, or to [mailbox@agencytool.com](mailto:mailbox@agencytool.com).

It's time to build robots.

launches.title: Molagri: Resistance-free pesticides 🪲
launches.tagline: Species-specific biopesticides built from engineered insect viruses, updatable the moment pests develop resistance.
launches.body:
**TLDR:** We build next-generation pesticides from engineered insect virus-like particles. They target a single pest species, stay safe for humans, pollinators, and the environment, and can be reprogrammed over time as pests evolve resistance.

Pesticides underpin modern agriculture and food security, accounting for $80B in annual spend. Without effective pesticides, we can't grow enough food.

<https://youtu.be/6rxXDJeC14Y>

**The Problem 🌱**

Pests are developing resistance faster than new pesticides can be invented to replace the failing ones. At the same time, regulators are banning core active ingredients over environmental and human toxicity. Farmers are losing tools from both ends at once.

**Our Solution 🪲**

We build pesticides out of insect virus-like particles. We start with a virus that only infects insects and is harmless to humans. We strip out its genome so it can't infect or replicate, and we keep the empty protein shell as a delivery vehicle.

We engineer that shell with two parts:

* A **targeting element** that recognizes a single pest species (or a set of species). This is what keeps the product species-specific and invisible to humans, pollinators, and beneficial insects.
* A **payload** that kills the pest.

Both parts are swappable. Changing the targeting element will modify which pest it kills. Changing the payload will result in a new kill mechanism for the same pest, which is how we update the product when resistance appears.

Designing for true pollinator safety is hard, so we did the underlying science ourselves. We solved a cryo-EM structure of a key receptor in honey bees, which lets us deliberately engineer our targeting elements so they do not bind pollinators.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108796&key=user_uploads/2273508/62f4362a-1938-4843-ab26-c9a62c742a84)

**Why Us? 🧑🏽‍🔬**

We are Zaky and Min, viral structural biology PhD candidates and lab mates at the University of Toronto, where we have worked together for the past 6 years studying how viruses interact with their hosts. We have published in Nature Microbiology and Nature Communications, and Min holds the world record for the highest-resolution structure of a coronavirus spike protein.

**Traction 📈**

We have signed our first grower LOI, have more in the pipeline, and produced our first set of viruses for testing. During the batch we also solved a cryo-EM structure of a honey-bee receptor that directly informs our pollinator-safe design.

**Connect with us!**

* **Growers and producers**: if you are fighting resistant pests or losing tools to bans, we would love to talk about your crops and target pests. Reach us at [molagri.com](http://molagri.com) 
* **Everyone else:** intros to ag and crop-science operators, or anyone who has built regulated biological products, are always welcome.

launches.title: 6thSense — Giving Robots Touch
launches.tagline: Giving Robots Touch
launches.body:
6thSense builds wearable tactile sensing rigs that capture how human hands interact with the world — pressure, contact, grip, and pose — across touch, vision, depth, force, and 3D hand pose, all in real environments. We sell that multimodal data to the companies training the next generation of dexterous robots.\
\
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gXx53tcIv5U>

Robots are getting good at seeing. They're still terrible at touching. That's because there's almost no data capturing what a hand actually feels while doing real tasks in real homes. Lab data doesn't cut it. We go anywhere and capture the missing layer that manipulation models need to learn fine motor control.

What makes our data different is the hardware we built to collect it. Our tactile sensing devices are designed and manufactured in-house, purpose-built to capture the richest touch signal in the industry — with scale in mind from the very beginning, enabling us to actually solve the tactile data problem. Every sensor maps directly to how robotic skin needs to work: a 1-to-1 analog for the tactile arrays going into the next generation of robot hands. That means the data we collect today doesn't just train better policies. It transfers directly to the hardware it's meant to run on. The team comes from Tesla, Mecka, Samsung, DoorDash, and Amazon, with expertise across hardware, sensors, ML, robotics, and software at scale. If you're training a manipulation policy or need custom tactile data, reach out.

We manufacture Nori: A sub-$2000 bimanual mobile manipulator that can clean rooms, restock shelves, and fold clothes. Nori can handle basic tasks out of the box, and its software lets anyone teach Nori to automate work specific to their home or business. 

Nori aims to solve the robotics data bottleneck. By deploying affordable robots to customers around the world, we can gather the diverse data required to train the next generation of generalist robotic policies. Every user of Nori makes Nori smarter.

Since launching 6 weeks ago we have already deployed our first robot and have over $440k+ in sales.

We can bring general-purpose robotics to homes and businesses that could never afford it before. There are 132.7 million households and 8.4 million employer business locations in the U.S. At $1,688 per robot, selling just one Nori to 0.5% of them represents a $1.2B market opportunity in the U.S. alone.
one_liner: The most capable American-made humanoid robot for $1,688

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
Robots are finally capable enough to be useful, but they're priced like cars, not appliances. A capable humanoid costs $20,000+, so general-purpose robots stay in labs and pilots instead of homes. 

It's a big problem because household labor is one of the largest unpriced markets in the world. Today's answer is a stack of single-task machines, a dishwasher, a washer, a vacuum, each $600 to $1,000 and doing exactly one thing. Whoever ships a general-purpose robot at appliance prices doesn't win a niche, they open consumer robotics the way the PC opened computing.

We're robotics researchers from Columbia (RoboPIL, CGUI). After years watching \[$100K research robots struggle with tasks cheap hardware could handle\], we realized the gap between lab robots and home robots isn't intelligence, it's cost discipline. Nobody was going to fix that from inside a lab, so we left to build it: a $1,688 robot anyone can teach.

name: Aerogen Systems
long_description:
We are building the future of chip manufacturing.

Chips are more advanced than ever, and the features inside them keep getting smaller. But the cleanroom infrastructure supporting their manufacture has not scaled at the same pace. Intel, TSMC, Samsung, and others spend billions building and operating massive cleanrooms, only to isolate their most advanced wafers from the surrounding facility as much as possible.

We think that architecture is backwards. Instead of making the entire building cleaner, why not make the machinery itself as clean as possible?

Talos is our proprietary tool-integrated purification system. It sits directly inside semiconductor equipment and continuously destroys airborne molecular contaminants before they reach the wafer. Instead of fighting contamination by constantly flooding tools with ultra-high-purity nitrogen, Talos keeps the environment inside the machine 10–100x cleaner, without the massive purge-gas bill.

Talos is powerful on its own, but it is also the foundation for a much bigger vision: the Cleanpipe.

The Aerogen Systems Cleanpipe is an ultra-clean interconnect infrastructure that protects wafers as they move from machine to machine across the fab. Rather than relying on a billion-dollar cleanroom to protect every cubic foot of factory space, Cleanpipe creates a controlled environment only where cleanliness actually matters: around the wafer.

Talos cleans the tools. Cleanpipe connects them. Eventually, we delete the cleanroom and build more advanced chips, at greater scale, with radically less infrastructure. With cleanpipes connecting tools, chip fabs can exist anywhere.
one_liner: Modernizing Chip Manufacturing Infrastructure

launches.title: Aerogen Systems: Building Chip Fabs Without Cleanrooms
launches.tagline: Redefining the architecture behind chip manufacturing
launches.body:
Hi YC!

We’re [Noah](https://www.linkedin.com/in/noahvogel/) and [Colin](https://www.linkedin.com/in/colin-lavery-67b7512a3/), the founders of [Aerogen Systems](https://www.aerogensystems.com/). We’re building the next generation of clean infrastructure for chip manufacturing.

**TL;DR:** Aerogen Systems makes semiconductor tools clean themselves. Talos, our tool-integrated purification system, continuously destroys airborne contaminants around the wafer, creating 10–100x cleaner tool environments while reducing dependence on ultra-high-purity nitrogen. Over time, Talos becomes the foundation for the Cleanpipe, an ultra-clean interconnect network that lets wafers move between tools without depending on the surrounding cleanroom.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5yBzBCzwFV8>

# **The Problem**

**Chip features keep getting smaller, but cleanrooms do not scale with them.**

Semiconductor manufacturers spend billions building enormous cleanroom facilities, then spend even more trying to isolate their most advanced wafers from the environment they just built.

As features approach the atomic scale, trace airborne contaminants that were once tolerable can create defects, reduce yield, and disrupt some of the most sensitive manufacturing processes on Earth. Yet the industry's answer has largely been more of the same: cleaner facilities, more filtration, and more ultra-high-purity nitrogen flooding sensitive equipment.

**The proof is in the yield numbers.** 2026 reporting puts Intel’s 18A program between roughly 50% and 65% yield as it pushed the node toward high-volume production. With global semiconductor sales projected to reach **$1.5 trillion** in 2026, every percentage point matters. Improvements in yield and manufacturing efficiency can represent tens of billions of dollars in value.

# **The Solution**

At Aerogen Systems, we think the industry is approaching this problem backwards.

**The whole factory does not need to be a massive cleanroom.** Only the environment immediately surrounding the wafer does.

Talos is our proprietary, tool-integrated purification system. It sits directly inside semiconductor manufacturing equipment and continuously recirculates and purifies the environment around the wafer. Instead of constantly replacing contaminated gas with more ultra-high-purity nitrogen, Talos destroys contaminants at the point of use, offering 10–100x cleaner tool environments while dramatically reducing dependence on purge gas and consumable filtration.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111026&key=user_uploads/3388722/a095a4e2-31a2-4307-b8f1-bca417cb27d7)

_1. Rendering of standalone Talos unit._

But Talos is only part of the vision.

With tool-integrated purification units as a foundation, we build **the Cleanpipe: ultra-clean interconnect infrastructure** that protects wafers as they move from machine to machine across the fab. Talos cleans the tools. The Cleanpipe connects tools to each other. Together, they delete the cleanroom and all the expenses that come with it.

# **What We’ve Built**

Talos has progressed through multiple generations of hardware development and is protected by patent-pending IP. We’ve validated the core purification architecture and are now working toward tool integrations, pilots, and commercial deployments with semiconductor manufacturers and equipment companies.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111026&key=user_uploads/3388722/a8596c2c-c29b-4271-8d92-85672dce0dc1)

_2. Test results showing Talos bringing industry-standard 6N purification levels down to 8N — a 100x improvement in cleanliness._

The next step is connecting these purified environments together through the Cleanpipe, creating an ultra-clean path around the wafer from tool to tool and ultimately removing the need to maintain the entire fab as one enormous cleanroom.

# **The Team**

Aerogen Systems started as a NASA-backed research group at the University of Michigan, where our team developed the underlying purification technology. 

We have spent the last several years designing, testing, patenting, and rebuilding this technology for extreme manufacturing environments.

* Noah, CEO, worked in manufacturing engineering at SpaceX, where he focused on production rate and yield improvement for the Starship program.


* Colin, CTO, previously built advanced particle detectors at H3D and led the team through the earliest design cycles of Talos.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111026&key=user_uploads/3388722/4db2a255-30a8-44ee-928b-b07425918094)

# **Our Ask**

We want to meet semiconductor fabs, equipment OEMs, and manufacturing teams interested in pilots, tool integrations, and commercial deployments. If this sounds like you, please reach out to [hi@aerogensystems.com](mailto:hi@aerogensystems.com)!

We are building toward a world where fabs no longer need billion-dollar cleanrooms to manufacture the world’s most advanced chips.

launches.body:
[Greypoint Industries (YC S26) Launch Video](https://youtu.be/y9jC4A7Fg04)

Greypoint Industries builds drone swarms that find enemy drone operators on the battlefield.

Over 70% of casualties in Ukraine come from drones. The entire defense space is focused on building interceptors to shoot them down. While they’re treating the symptom, we’re going after the root cause: the drone stations. They’re hidden in bunkers, behind terrain, and fly the drones that kill our warfighters and civilians. Today, soldiers have no way to reliably geolocate operators on the battlefield.

Greypoint Industries built LEGION, a drone swarm that identifies, geolocates, and tracks every emitter on the battlefield using the enemy’s own radio signals. LEGION enables our warfighters to precisely track previously obscured targets like jammers, command posts, and drone operators so they can proactively respond to threats instead of reacting to them.

Greypoint has just won a contract with the Canadian Government, demoed with the Armed Forces, and successfully geolocated a target using their aerial platform. The founding team brings experience from the Canadian Infantry, General Dynamics, Bosch Quantum Sensing, and TerraSense Analytics.

Defend the West. Deploy Greypoint.\
\
Find out more at <https://greypointindustries.com>.
