launches.title: Neuromorphic - Building an embodiment-agnostic “brain” that makes robots fast to deploy
launches.tagline: We make robots smarter, and faster to deploy. Starting with wet labs!
launches.body:
Hi everyone! We’re Cem, Ege, and Vatan, the founders of Neuromorphic 👋\
\
**TL;DR** Neuromorphic is building an embodiment-agnostic “brain” that makes robots fast to deploy, and easy to manage through natural interfaces like Slack, email, and phone. Our goal is to make deploying robots in wet labs and other physical industries as easy as onboarding a new employee.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6T0BDyjakmo>\
\
**The Problem**\
To make robotics mainstream, we believe two problems have to be resolved:\
1\. Deployment: Robots are still too slow, expensive, and engineering-intensive to deploy and adapt to new tasks and environments.\
2\. Interaction: Managing and controlling robots remains too technical.\
\
**What We’ve Built**\
Neuromorphic packages sensors, compute, and software into a “brain” that can be attached to any robot body. An onboard LLM orchestrator turns natural-language instructions into workflows made up of reusable robotic skills, such as navigating, picking up an object, opening a refrigerator, or inspecting an area. Individual skills can be of various types; they could be AI models we develop, like Vision-Language Models and Video Action Models, or just plain code. Sensor-based safety loops monitor every action to ensure reliable execution.

We are also giving robots emails, phone numbers, and Slack access to make human-robot interaction more intuitive than using dashboards. The robots then respond to queries and take actions using the onboard LLM.\
\
**Traction**\
Within a week of our first conversation with a leading biotechnology company, we deployed our robot in their wet lab, which is capable of operating autonomously 24/7, and already completed over 1500 tasks.\
\
**The Team**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109550&key=user_uploads/3607343/b28b023b-f328-4c5d-9181-720e96e5b1a3)

\
Cem: Second-time founder and did robotics research at Cambridge University. Previously built LLM routing and training acceleration, and did precision robotics.\
\
Vatan: Maintained multiple open-source robotics libraries, most notably MoveIt, one of the most popular motion-planning frameworks for robotics. Led various teams in robotics startups from Series A to Series C in Japan and Singapore. Deployed over a thousand robots.\
\
Ege: Did Robotics and AI research at Bilkent University. Research fellow at Nanyang Technological University. Published research in top AI and robotics conferences. Won HackMIT in 2024.\
\
Cem and Ege first met as teammates in the FIRST Robotics Competition. They reached out to Vatan for mentorship and robotics advice. We spent the next three years building robots and winning competitions together. We remained close and eventually reunited to start Neuromorphic!\
\
**Ask**\
We're looking for warm intros to wet lab, biotech, and physical-industry operators. If you have a repetitive physical process and have wondered whether a robot could do it, email us at [founders@neuromorphic.vision](mailto:founders@neuromorphic.vision) or [book a call here](https://cal.com/team/neuromorphic/meet-the-founders-of-neuromorphic).

launches.body:
<https://youtu.be/uey-UwwKSw8>

**TL;DR:** Neuron is building the world's first purpose built industrial controller for AI, replacing the antiquated PLCs running every machine and factory. We compress controls projects from weeks to hours, from chemical processing to nuclear reactors.

We have hardware ready to deploy today, hit us up for a pilot!

**Problem**

Every piece of industrial equipment, conveyors, pumps, packaging cells, process plants, runs on PLCs. But PLCs got stuck in the 90s: it's 2026 and you're paying $5000 for a controller with 5MB of memory, programmable only with esoteric IDEs and languages frozen in 1993. Reindustrialization and data center buildups are pushing demand up while the programmer workforce shrinks. Projects still cost a fortune and take months.

**Solution**

We're rebuilding the controller from first principles: state-of-the-art hardware, an AI-native stack, one ecosystem unifying PLC, HMI, SCADA, and Historian. Our agent contextualizes your requirements and hardware, then lets anyone program production applications in plain English, with test and verification guardrails and first-class data observability.

**Traction**

Our tech is in customers' plants today: pilots in chemical processing, electronics manufacturing, wastewater treatment, and small modular reactors.

**Team**

Dennis Ren (CEO): founding EE at Freeform, built the hardware stack for the world's most advanced metal 3D-printing factory. Apple Vision Pro founding team, Amazon Go, Tesla Fremont.

Kenneth Rhee (CTO): second-time founder, bootstrapped and exited WorkIPO. Custom ERP, MES, and CRM systems; ex-Amazon and GOAT Group (YC W11).

If you — or someone you know — build machines or factories that run on PLCs and HMIs, we'd love to talk: [hello@neuronindustries.com](mailto:hello@neuronindustries.com)

name: Ultrasonium
long_description:
The technologies that define this century, including data centers, rockets, satellites, and robots, are built from complex metal parts. As these systems advance, the parts get harder to make. Past a certain complexity, casting and machining stop working, and the advanced methods that remain are slow, expensive, and hazardous.

Ultrasonium has invented a new manufacturing method to make these critical parts 15x faster and 75% cheaper than the methods they replace, in the U.S. and at scale. Solid metal feedstock goes in and a finished part safely comes out, controlled by a physical AI layer and novel control processes. 

The systems that matter most, in aerospace, energy, and compute, are demanding metal geometries that can't be machined or cast and are too expensive and slow to make with incumbent methods, at a moment when domestic manufacturing capacity is a national priority.

Our founding team has built and innovated some of the most complex engineering systems known to man: quantum computers, superconductors, nuclear reactors, and novel aerospace alloy processing methods.

launches.body:
**Building the toughest super computers for earth and space**\
\
**TL;DR:** Data centers are stuck for years waiting for power, while delayed construction sites across the world sit on unused interconnects, losing $1B per week in the US alone, in interest on trillions of dollars of debt. Our pods deploy on those sites and generate revenue for them in days. They use diamond wafers in the cooling system so pods run anywhere on earth, even a desert.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rf8cCV6qFow>

**The deal**

If you need compute (GPU hours, tokens, capacity for a training run) send us a note. We sell short and long-term contracts below market rate.

If your data has to stay on-prem (**defense, CUI, CMMC)**, we sell managed, modular pods directly and are already working with large aerospace companies.

**We're building factories**

SpaceX didn't just build rockets, they built rocket factories. We do the same and our first factory stands up over the next few months, potentially funded by the state of Missouri. We vertically integrate the critical components that currently carry multi-year lead times: transformers, switchgear and power distribution, and by taking control of our own supply chain we ensure we can build pods fast enough.

**Financed like aircraft**

Our pods are financed like aircraft - debt at **\~5-6%, not 11-15%**. A data center is a risky construction loan: money stuck in a half-built site for years, and if it fails the lender holds a building and a pile of GPUs priced by a brutally volatile market - the banks are freaking out. Our pods leave the factory fully functional, earns the moment it's connected to power, and can be repossessed and redeployed: the profile of equipment finance, far faster and cheaper.

**Traction**

Today we have $95M in LOI’s for our hosted compute and a further $27M for direct sales of our pods. Our first two clusters go live in Missouri this month, followed by the first modular factory.

**Our asks**

* **Compute buyers and offtake.** We'd love to speak to anyone buying compute, or setting up on-prem deployments, or needing CMMC compliance. Introductions to procurement teams at OpenAI, Anthropic, or any startup constrained by access to cheap compute would be incredible.
* **Hiring.** Data center engineers, electrical engineers, any data center nerds you know.
* **Financiers.** These projects run on capital from infra investors and tech lenders. If you've worked in that world, we'd love to chat.
* **Construction sites.** If you sell to construction sites, work in construction, mining, or fab production, or own a site yourself - we will put a money machine on it. Let's chat.

**Join us as we build supercomputers for the galaxy!**

launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋! We're [Emil Ares](https://www.linkedin.com/in/emil-ares/) and [Gad Marconi](https://www.linkedin.com/in/gad-marconi/), co-founders of [Marengo](https://www.linkedin.com/company/marengox).

**TL;DR** $6.7T is going towards data center capex up to 2030. It still takes 10-12 months to design data centers. Marengo is _the engineering firm for accelerated data center development._ Site Due Diligence through FEED and permitting design in half the traditional time and half the cost. We’ve developed internal AI design tools that our professional engineers use to accelerate their engineering design work. Customers receive validated outputs they can trust. Already working with some of the largest developers in the world.

---

**Our Launch Video: [https://youtu.be/57EbJ0Buz-U](https://youtu.be/57EbJ0Buz-U)**

**Ask:** Are you a data center developer? Give us a site. Let Marengo show you what accelerated engineering looks like on one of your projects. Click [here](https://marengox.com/).

**The problem\[s\]:**

Huge **expenditure on design**: $6.7T of data center capex by 2030 - engineering design fees are a massive 12% of construction cost, meaning $800B in design spend alone.

Huge **time waste**: engineering design takes 12-36 months (feasibility, due diligence, FEED/permitting design, detailed design); it’s done manually, meaning a design firm can only handle 3-4 different concepts per site, leading to suboptimal designs, worse decisions and higher risk.

**The Solution:**

AI alone doesn’t have the engineering, know-how or trust to be effective here. A step change is needed. Marengo is needed.

launches.title: Cosmic Robotics: Autonomous construction on Earth and beyond
launches.tagline: Robotic construction equipment to build a city on Mars. We’re proving the technology by building large-scale infrastructure on Earth — utility-scale solar farms and hyperscale data centers.
launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋

We’re [James](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jamesemerick/) and [Lewis](https://www.linkedin.com/in/lewis-c-jones/) - co-founders of [Cosmic Robotics](https://www.cosmicrobotics.com). 

**TL;DR**

**We build robotic construction equipment to build a city on Mars**. We’re proving the technology today by building large-scale infrastructure on Earth – utility-scale solar farms and hyperscale data centers. Our first machine, Cosmic-1, has already installed tens of thousands of solar panels in the field and more than doubled the productivity of traditional crews.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_Dl00xlJbcI> 

**❌ The problem**

After working at NASA JPL, SpaceX, and Relativity Space, we believe rockets are no longer the limiting factor to space exploration and that the first humans will land on Mars by 2034. **The new bottleneck is construction**. We won't be sending thousands of construction workers to Mars to build the energy, compute, and housing needed to sustain even a small city. **It has to be built by robots that don't exist yet**.

On Earth we have a similar problem - **we’ve lost the ability to build**. Construction productivity has declined for 50 years while manufacturing and agriculture became 10-15x more productive through automation. **The missing technology is robotic manipulation for the tasks still done by hand**: lifting, placing, fastening.

Meanwhile, there is a generational infrastructure buildout happening right now. **$7 trillion** is going into AI data centers, power, and compute over the next six years, **more than the Apollo Program, Manhattan Project, and Interstate Highway System combined**. 40% of US data center projects are running behind schedule, and the skilled labor shortage is the #1 cause. 

**🤖 What we've built**

Cosmic-1 is a 10,000 lb autonomous robot capable of heavy-lift manipulation. In solar, it picks up 90 lb panels and places them onto racking with millimeter precision in any environment: 100-degree heat, freezing rain, snow, and dust. It seamlessly integrates into existing construction processes. Across tens of thousands of cycles it has more than doubled the labor productivity of solar installation, on some of the largest solar projects in the US.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106899&key=user_uploads/522502/bb5f86ec-a23b-4ffd-a173-87f36ce6fb1c)

**👬 The Team**

We come at this problem from two angles. James (CEO) grew up on construction sites, then spent his career bringing robots to the field with Built Robotics and Autodesk Research. He learned you don't change the oldest industry in the world by disrupting it; you earn your way in by giving crews better tools.

Lewis' (CTO) life ambition is to build a city on Mars. His work at NASA, SpaceX, and Relativity Space spans rocket engines, launch vehicles, satellites, space stations, and, yes, Martian robots. When it became clear the space industry was well on its way to Mars, he went looking for the construction robots. When he didn't find them, we started Cosmic.

We’ve brought together a team of industry experts with experience building robots, rockets, drones, self-driving cars, humanoids, and nuclear reactor operations. We know what it takes to get a machine to show up day-in-day-out on the jobsite.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106899&key=user_uploads/522502/87f30a8e-6f83-490e-8bef-04225d1a525e)

**🚀 What's next**

We're scaling in solar, taking Cosmic-1 into data center construction, and working with NASA on lunar construction robotics. Revenue and data from deployments on Earth train the systems we'll deploy on Mars.

**🙏 Our asks**

1. **Know a hyperscaler or neocloud construction team?** Please connect us.
2. **Share this post** and [follow our journey](https://www.linkedin.com/company/cosmic-robotics/).

👉 Contact us at [james@cosmicrobotics.com](mailto:james@cosmicrobotics.com) | [cosmicrobotics.com](http://cosmicrobotics.com)

launches.body:
**Hey YC!**

We're Rohan, Dev, and Tommy, and we're building Praxis.

**Praxis turns real-world work into training data for robots.**

<https://youtu.be/xri7vyzxW-I?si=L6ZBgLO24OrvYuuH>

**What we do**

Robots learn to act in the physical world by watching humans do the work. We partner with businesses to capture egocentric human demonstration data, the first-person video of how tasks actually get done in factories, warehouses, homes, and other physical work environments, then supply it to the labs and humanoid teams training the next generation of robots. Robotics data is our focus, but since our collection infrastructure overlaps, we're happy to explore other multimodal data too.

**The problem**

Robotics is missing its internet-scale training corpus. LLMs learned from the web, books, code, and the accumulated record of human thought. Robots need the equivalent record of human action: how people pick, pack, clean, assemble, inspect, cook, use tools, recover from mistakes, and move through messy physical environments.

Collecting some of this data is easy. Collecting enough of the right kind is brutally hard, for two reasons.

First, diversity is capped by access. Models only generalise if they've seen the full range of real environments and operators, from a one-person shop to a national-scale industrial operation. Getting in the door across that entire spectrum, and across continents, is a physical-world access problem that most teams can't solve.

Second, it takes two rare skills at once. You have to know what frontier labs need at a technical level, and be able to run demanding physical operations across thousands of real sites, standardising capture and turning fragmented workflows into model-ready data. Few teams have both halves.

**Our solution**

We already run collections across 150 environment types on 5 continents, with diversity from mom-and-pop stores to conglomerates accounting for 3% of a nation's GDP, and a reachable network of 60,000 workers. Depending on the task, we capture egocentric video, stereo-RGB, IMU, wrist-camera views, glove kinematics, haptics, and dense annotations. Everything is delivered calibrated, synced, pose-tracked, QA'd, and PII-scrubbed. We build and deploy custom capture hardware quickly because part of the team operates out of Shenzhen.

**Why us**

Praxis is built to do both hard things at once. We pair robotics research depth (IEEE, NASA JPL) with the ability to actually run demanding operations in the real world, from Fortune 500 supply chains to Parliaments, plus a Shenzhen hardware team. That combination- technical understanding of what labs need plus real physical-world access at scale- is what lets us deliver diverse, model-ready data at a cost and breadth that is irreplaceable.

**Our asks**

1. Intros to anyone working on robotics, embodied AI, or world-models, especially data and research leads. If you need other forms of multimodal data, we're happy to explore that too.
2. If you run a business with interesting physical work (logistics, manufacturing, food, retail, or lab work) and would like to monetize it, we'd love to talk.

You can reach us at [founders@praxisrobotics.io](mailto:founders@praxisrobotics.io) and [rohan@praxisrobotics.io](mailto:rohan@praxisrobotics.io)[ https://www.praxisrobotics.io](https://www.praxisrobotics.io)

launches.title: Skymerse: Autopilot for Flight Operations
launches.tagline: From planning and monitoring in the operations center to real-time support in the cockpit.
launches.body:
I’m Damian, founder of Skymerse (S26). I’m a licensed flight dispatcher and have spent 10 years working across flight operations, aviation data, and software.

We’re building one AI system to automate flight operations - from planning and monitoring in the operations center to real-time support in the cockpit.

Our goal is full automation of the work behind every flight.

<https://youtu.be/czP5N1FJ1ds>

## The problem

Airlines have spent decades digitizing flight operations. The information moved from paper to screens. The work of understanding it did not. A flight exists across many systems. Each system may be good at its own job, but the complete operational picture exists between them.

Pilots and operations teams still have to build that picture themselves. They search, compare, and interpret information to plan, monitor, and adapt every flight from schedule to landing.

When something changes, they do it again. When responsibility moves from the operations center to the crew, much of the context has to be passed on or rebuilt.

Today, people are the integration layer.

## What Skymerse does

Skymerse builds a live operational model of every flight. When an airline’s schedule flows in, it assembles the operational context for each flight and keeps it current as conditions change.

That model is the foundation for automation. Skymerse does not stop at displaying information or sending an alert. It understands what a change means for the flight, updates the operation, and carries the required work forward automatically.

Skymerse plans, monitors, and adapts flights from the operations center to the cockpit. Instead of rebuilding context across tools and handoffs, Skymerse manages each flight as one continuous process, from schedule to landing.

## Why I started Skymerse

Skymerse started with [Notamify.com](http://Notamify.com). I built Notamify because I was amazed by how much information pilots and ops teams have to process before every flight - and how much of that work was still done by hand.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111421&key=user_uploads/1472269/7e9fe835-e22f-4cb1-92dc-ac0f99a0cce2)

Notamify interprets every single NOTAM into operational impact. It reduces the briefing time from 2 hours to 2 minutes per flight. It now serves airline customers and thousands of pilots and aviation professionals.

As we built it, the larger problem became clear. Making one source easier interpreted is valuable, but people still have to connect it with the rest of the operation. They still have to work out what it means for their flight and what to do next.

Skymerse is that next step: from helping people understand one part of a flight to automating flight operations e2e.

## Automate your flight operations

We are onboarding airlines that want to automate their flight operations. If you lead flight operations, dispatch, or an OCC, we want to show you Skymerse on your flights.

[Book a demo](http://skymerse.com/demo) or email [hello@skymerse.com](mailto:hello@skymerse.com).

launches.title: Grip - Robotics for Waste Management
launches.tagline: Robots that sort any waste and recover recyclables, learning from every grasp.
launches.body:
Hi everyone - Stan and Jonas here, founders of **Grip**. We build intelligent robots that sort _any_ waste, not just the clean, predictable objects existing systems are limited to. We're starting with plastic contamination in organic waste.\
\
<https://youtu.be/qIJ4a49WxpI>

**The problem**

We didn't start with a thesis, we found it on sorting lines, after visiting waste facilities across several countries:

* **Contamination is existential.** Plastic that organic-waste facilities can't remove gets shredded, processed, and spread onto agricultural soil. Operators spend up to 30% of operating costs fighting it and still fall short. Even Germany's 0.1% limit for plastic in finished compost is a tacit admission that full removal isn't possible with today's tools.
* **The labor force is aging and shrinking.** The picking work is unpleasant and turnover is brutal. Operators increasingly aren't choosing between people and robots. They're choosing between robots and nobody.
* **Dangerous items cause fires.** Batteries, propane tanks, and vapes slip through and ignite during handling and shredding: 448 reported fires at US and Canadian waste facilities in 2025, \~$2.5B in damage, and insurers are walking away. At the same time trash sorting is sitting in the top 5 of US deadliest occupations.

**What we built**

The hard part isn't the gripper. It's that waste never looks the way you planned. Objects arrive crushed, folded, tangled, half-buried, and moving. Put today's sorting robots in front of this and they break.

We're building one manipulation system that picks whatever shows up, at the front of the line where the material is most chaotic and existing automation stops. That means chaotic scene understanding, robust grasp planning, and hardware built for real waste streams: our custom three-way gripper is designed to maximize throughput, taking out as much contamination per cycle as possible.

Our rugged hardware matters, but intelligence is the product. Every pick generates data no other system ever encounters: what the robot saw, what it tried, how the material responded, whether it worked.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111317&key=user_uploads/3678142/bc867fdc-9225-4b85-83f9-f83433465d5b)

**Why now**

Waste policy has moved from vague ambition to enforceable deadlines:

* Separate bio-waste collection is now mandatory across the EU. More material, and more contamination, every year.
* New EU fertiliser rules just cut permitted impurities in compost and digestate, with national limits like Germany's stricter still.
* The US is real: California mandated a 75% cut in landfilled organics, missed it, and enforcement is ramping. At the same time, landfills near major cities are filling up, and that pressure is pushing more and more US municipalities to collect organic waste separately. More material, more contamination, more facilities that need to sort it.

More than 6,500 biowaste plants and thousands of recycling facilities across Europe and North America face this with no robot that can touch it. That's Grip.

**Why us**

We've built autonomous race cars, quadrupeds, drones, and excavators, robots that operate in dirt, weather, and chaos rather than controlled labs. Grip is that experience applied to an industry where physical intelligence removes a real bottleneck.

**Our ask**

We'd love intros to:

* Owners and operators of composting, anaerobic-digestion, and organic-waste facilities
* Owners and operators of MRFs and recycling facilities
* Regulators and experts shaping contamination limits and recycling standards

If someone runs a facility and will show us their hardest sorting problem, we'll get on a plane.

launches.title: Hop Aero 🚀 Rocket Cargo
launches.tagline: Hop Aero delivers an autonomous 21st century D-Day
launches.body:
[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1xqm08Bpwv1LXOsas-oVfZ5rDwp1lNqP8](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1xqm08Bpwv1LXOsas-oVfZ5rDwp1lNqP8/view?usp=share_link)
\
❌ **Problem**

While Jacob was serving in the U.S. Marine Corps, Typhoon Haiyan had just swept through the Philippines. Jacob and his unit were given a clear order: deliver life-saving supplies of medicine and food as soon as possible. Despite working around the clock, the effort was regularly blocked due to aircraft breaking down, flight-critical parts being out of inventory, and pilot fatigue.

Similarly, when building his previous startup, Matija’s team were given 24 hours’ notice to deliver a satellite propulsion system to the mission integrator. FedEx and UPS could not guarantee on-time delivery, forcing Matija to make a 23-hour trip to hand-deliver the flight hardware. He spent the flight back thinking that there has to be a better way.

It turned out that it wasn’t just us. Everyone from startups to the U.S. military, needs faster delivery. We saw an opportunity to create the fastest form of transportation in the world.

🚀 **Rockets are the answer**

We are building Rook, an autonomous rocket that delivers 250 kg of cargo up to 750 km away. That’s Okinawa to Taiwan in 15 minutes.

Rook launches from a standard 40-ft shipping container, flies through space, re-enters at hypersonic speeds and lands on unprepared surfaces, allowing it to launch and land anywhere on the planet. This opens up completely new commercial markets and military capabilities.

Rook can deliver swarms of autonomous unmanned systems to the battlefield, delivering a fully-autonomous 21st century D-Day effect for the U.S. and allies. The same Rook can deliver time-critical goods for manufacturing, automotive, aerospace, offshore oil and pharma, preventing downtime costs of up to $2M/hour.

🏆 **Traction**

* **Won a $1.25M DoW contract** from the US Air Force.
* **Completed our first tethered test** at the Oklahoma spaceport on a small-scale prototype
* **Successfully hot-fired our engine and igniter** built using hopOS, our AI-augmented secret sauce.
* **Successfully demonstrated drone deployment** from our rocket cargo vehicle.

🥷 **Team**

**Matija (CEO):** Previously founded porkchop (electric propulsion for small satellites) - launched on SpaceX Transporter-3, built a $400M+ sales pipeline, sold the IP. Led a 20+ person supersonic UAV team at Destinus and scaled Ukrainian loitering-munition production from 10 to 100+ units/month.

**Jacob (CTO):** US Marine Corps (MV-22 avionics) → SpaceX (Falcon 9/Heavy; built the OG booster refurb program) → Virgin Orbit (LauncherOne) → Masten (led systems integration & test on NASA's CLPS lunar lander) → SpinLaunch. A decade of making rockets fly on schedule.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112220&key=user_uploads/480112/8946bdbe-09b5-447f-8022-6233e2401800)

🙏 **Asks**

* **Intros to DoW customers and end-users.** Anyone with warm paths into the Navy, PACOM, or program offices working contested logistics - we want to talk.
* **Intros to commercial end-users.** Businesses with high downtime costs such as manufacturing, automotive, aerospace, offshore oil, pharma - all are right down our alley.
* **Payload partners.** We want to deploy your drones, interceptors, electronic warfare jammers and more! Reach out if you want to give your product the ability to teleport to the battlefield!

launches.title: Hebbian Robotics - APIs for searching and analyzing Physical AI data at scale
launches.tagline: We enable evaluation of data quality without training a robotics model
launches.body:
# \*\*\*\*

**TLDR;**

* **Hebbian Robotics builds APIs for searching and analyzing Physical AI data at scale**
* Our APIs enable data providers to get **on-demand signals and metrics** on the quality of their data, without managing infrastructure
* We help our customers evaluate data quality without training a robotics model

<https://youtu.be/ffvFNs3bjbs>

**Our Ask**

* Buyers want data they can trust. If you're selling egocentric or robot data, **Let’s Chat ([https://calendly.com/brandon-hebbianrobotics/30min](https://calendly.com/brandon-hebbianrobotics/30min)**) and we'll show you how quality signals and metrics help you sell more at higher prices
* **Check out Pareto ([https://pareto.hebbianrobotics.com/](https://pareto.hebbianrobotics.com/)),** an example of how our APIs can be used

### **Who We Are**

* We’re Brandon and Kingston, we've trained AI models for industrial cleaning robots and built production systems for camera fleets across the globe
* [**Brandon Ong**](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/388120)'s previous AI startup was backed by Sequoia. He did research on AI for low resource languages that topped Stanford’s LLM benchmark, SEA-HELM, and dropped out of his joint PhD in Robotics at Columbia and NTU
* [**Kingston Kuan**](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/968709) spent years at Jane Street building systems that scaled to millions of messages per second. At Verkada, he worked on their core video surveillance platform that processed large scale multimodal data

### **The Problem**

* **High quality data is the bottleneck for unlocking the next frontier of intelligence in robotics**
* Buyers want **data they can trust** 
* Data providers don’t have the bandwidth to provide signals and metrics about the quality of their data when they are **focused on** **operational excellence**  
* This means that **model developers are forgoing model improvements due to a lack of high quality data**, impeding progress in robotics

### **Our Solution**

* APIs for searching and analyzing Physical AI data at scale that enables providers to get **on-demand signals and metrics on data quality**
* Buyers demanding per-collector hour limits? **Prove compliance while we stay ahead of the workarounds**
* Changed standard operating procedures for collection? **Monitor for quality drift and regression**
* Suspect duplicate samples? **Verify quickly with a single API call**
* Our APIs enable **evaluation of data quality without training a robotics model, fast iteration cycles for** high quality data collection, and unlock **model improvements** 

### **How to reach us**

* We want to support data providers who believe in collecting high quality data in an ethical way
* To get started, email [**brandon.ong@hebbianrobotics.com**](mailto:brandon.ong@hebbianrobotics.com)

launches.title: Earendil | Autonomous Air Defence
launches.tagline: Autonomous, combat-proven interceptors for defending against drone swarms.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** We build autonomous interceptors that kill drones for less than the cost of the threat. Aeglos is in active operational use and has scored operational intercepts. The team has hundreds of confirmed combat intercepts. Looking for introductions to NATO-aligned air defence and C-UAS leads.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kZmj9NTDALo>

**The problem**:

Air defence economics are broken. A Patriot interceptor costs $3-7 million and is routinely used against $50,000 drones. Production rates of a few hundred units a year make these systems too scarce and too expensive for the volume of low-cost threats now in the air. They should be reserved for high-value targets.

Exactly like the Sherman tank versus the Tiger: it does not matter how good the system is if there are more threats than ammunition.

**What we do**:

Aeglos is a high-speed autonomous interceptor designed end-to-end for the mass drone problem: airframe, autonomy software, and operator model. The operator clicks launch, then selects the intercept in software. No stage of flight requires a pilot and no flying experience is needed. One operator can control up to 64 interceptors. Engagement cost stays below the price of the drone being destroyed.

Most C-UAS offerings are a single interceptor airframe. Operators still need skilled pilots, long training pipelines, and constant attention during the engagement. We built the complete system so any operator can achieve consistent intercepts without those requirements. The result is a system that can be fielded at the small-unit and critical-infrastructure level without the specialist crews or multi-million-dollar missiles that current layered air defence relies on.

Aeglos is operationally deployed, radar-agnostic, manufactured in Europe, and NDAA-compliant with no Chinese components.

**Why us:**

The entire team is ex-military with frontline Ukrainian experience, primarily in elite units and air defence. Collectively, we have hundreds of confirmed drone intercepts across multiple systems. We designed Aeglos from that experience - in the same contested Ukrainian airspace where most Western systems have not yet been stress-tested at scale.

[\@James Walton](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/3723601): British Army and UAS expert with frontline Ukrainian experience who has previously run companies.

[\@Dan Komorny](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/3723983):  A decade of experience in Drones and Security directly in Ukraine. Serial entrepreneur with multiple startups under his belt.

The Team: Commandos, Airborne, Special Forces and Air Defense veterans.

**Ask**

Introductions to air defence and C-UAS leads in NATO-aligned militaries, national acquisition teams, and operators responsible for protecting forward positions and critical infrastructure.

We are also open to partnerships with complementary companies.

launches.body:
**TL;DR**

**Team**

Brogan was employee #23 at SpaceX. He built the first Falcon and Dragon. Previously, he founded Hyperloop and Arrivo.

Ross is a lunar geologist from the Colorado School of Mines. He previously founded the Planetary Sunshade Institute.

**Problem**

There is infinite power in space. But rockets can’t carry enough solar panels. Rockets are the constraint.

<https://youtu.be/PsxbpAYPtDY>

**Solution**

Power in space must be made in space. Self replicating power and mass relieves the rocket constraint.

The Moon is made of Silicon (and other useful atoms). Silicon makes solar panels (and compute). Solar panels make energy, to refine more silicon and power more compute.

<https://youtu.be/SZjJQqCew70>

**Traction**

* Completed NASA contract
* $1B LOIs from multiple customers
* Going to the Moon in 2028

**Why now**

Capital needs from Earth will diminish as self-replicating power and mass grows on the Moon. Moving up the Kardashev scale will be a matter of wattage and tonnage, not dollars. If you’re not early to self-replication, you’re too late.

launches.title: Dawn Industries - Automatic Diagnosis & Fix for Industrial Automation
launches.tagline: AI that understands the entire industrial cell and stages the fix in minutes.
launches.body:
Hey BF 👋 We are [@Joohyun (CJ) Cha](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/1720857) and [@Robin Lee](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2574843), cofounders of [@Dawn Industries](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/33344). We’re building **VIM**, Automatic Diagnosis & Fix for Industrial Automation Cells.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109744&key=user_uploads/2574843/10398df4-83d1-4d24-860a-5ede83b91f9c)

# **TL;DR:**

**VIM is Sentry for industrial automation cells. When a cell faults, VIM reads the error code and the live machine signals, digs the root cause out of the OEM manuals and the cell's own history, and stages one safe fix for the operator to approve. When a CNC drifts, VIM catches it with the machine's own probe seconds after the cut and stages the offset correction. Downtime goes from hours to about a minute; scrap gets caught at part one instead of final inspection.**

Watch how **VIM** works:

Robot Cell Video: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JfGQjorNS2U>

CNC Machine Video: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fgNPOtBLku8>

# WHAT WE BUILT

VIM sits on the cell and closes the loop from fault to recovery:

1. **Connect**. Reads **PLC**, **HMI**, **robot**, **CNC**, **sensor**, and **driver state** without touching the controls you already trust.
2. **Understand**. Matches the fault to live signals, the right page of the right manual, and this cell's own prior recoveries or trends the probe touches and traces drift to tool wear, thermal growth, a bumped fixture.
3. **Recover**. Stages one bounded, validated action: a restart, a parameter change, an offset correction. The operator approves it like a pull request.

Before anything moves, the safety chain is verified: interlocks, light curtain, area scanner. VIM cannot bypass it; that's a precondition in the action policy, not a feature. And when the fault is genuinely hardware, VIM routes the incident to the right person with the exact diagnosis and repair steps attached, instead of a generic alarm and a prayer.

**Autonomy is earned, not assumed**: VIM ships read-only, then one-click approval, then unattended recovery only on fault classes where it has earned trust. And it's mixed-vendor by design (FANUC robots and CNC controls, Universal Robots, Siemens, Allen-Bradley, Cognex, Keyence, Renishaw probes), because a cell is multi-vendor by definition and a copilot that speaks one vendor's language can't close the loop.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109744&key=user_uploads/2574843/83b531fe-5737-4f94-8b70-cd37330dae7c)

# TEAM

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109744&key=user_uploads/2574843/df76af6e-3516-4d76-9081-145424822ef3)

We're four people covering both halves of the problem.

[Robin Lee](https://www.linkedin.com/in/robinlee02/) and [Joohyun (CJ) Cha](https://www.linkedin.com/in/joohyun-cha), cofounders, Robin was the founding AI engineer at an aviation AI startup, and built the production AI systems behind its $10M Series A and a 1st-place Minister's Award from Korea's Ministry of Science and ICT. CJ cofounded Zipper as CTO (acquired by MetaZone), did ML on genomic data at Avalo. We spent the past years in plants and machine shops learning all the faults and error that happen during manufacturing processes.

Our founding engineers, come from Tesla and robotics research labs. They spent years building and fixing automation cells and various robot cases.

# OUR ASK

* **Intros to plant managers, manufacturing engineers, and controls engineers** at plants running robot cells (palletizing, case packing, welding, machine tending, inspection). If a stopped line ruins their week, we want to meet them.
* **Intros to machining and quality leaders at plants and shops (primarily aerospace & defense) running CNCs**, anywhere scrap gets discovered at final inspection instead of at the machine.
* **War stories.** Tell us about the cell that keeps stopping or the machine that keeps drifting. Best case, we make it your most reliable one.

Reach us at [joohyun_cha@dawnxr.com](mailto:joohyun_cha@dawnxr.com) or 401-226-3503, or book a demo at <https://dawnxr.com>.

name: Robocurve
long_description:
Robocurve builds open-source tools and independent benchmarks to measure how well robots can do real-world jobs. Instead of relying on unverified demo videos from frontier labs, we score their models on reproducible benchmarks that anyone can trust.

Today there are no well-run, standardized robotics benchmarks. Labs evaluate in-house, and no independent group has stepped in to run continuous benchmarking as a service. The result is that no one actually knows how good anyone else is, or where the real frontier sits.

Good benchmarks require operating and maintaining physical hardware and real-world setups. Simulation only goes so far, since models that look strong in sim can show large performance gaps once deployed in the real world. Building real-world benchmarks means coordinating job-domain experts, evals engineering, and hands-on robotics all at once.

Frontier labs are targeting general-purpose robotics by 2028, yet the field of robotics evals barely exists. Whoever builds the trusted measure of robot capability becomes the reference everyone relies on. We combine backgrounds in AI evals and robotics to build and grow this field as fast as possible. We already shipped v1 of our open-source framework, Inspect Robots, and ran our first pilot scoring a frontier model on a real robot.
one_liner: Evals for robots

founders.title: Founder/CEO

launches.title: Robocurve — Real-World Evaluations of Physical AI
launches.tagline: Real-world evals for robots
launches.body:
Hi, I’m [Jay](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jeqcho/), co-founder of [Robocurve](http://robocurve.org). We measure and reports what frontier robots can actually do in the real world.

Our launch video <https://youtu.be/Cjkt2ikvsiQ>

Frontier labs are racing to build general-purpose robots within two years, yet no one knows what today's robots are truly capable of. Demo videos of robots performing narrow, cherry-picked tasks proliferate, but there are no rigorous, continuous, standardized benchmarks for robotics.

Robocurve builds benchmarks for robots and the AI models that control them, to help the world understand how far robotics has come and how fast it's moving. Our benchmarks range from playing Jenga and making a sandwich to constructing a data center.

General-purpose robots could arrive before the end of the decade, with far-reaching implications: accelerated data center buildouts, explosive economic growth from a fully automated economy, and intensified geopolitical competition between the US and China. Real-world evaluations from Robocurve will help clarify the timeline to general-purpose robots so that society can prepare for their arrival well ahead of time.

[Jay](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jeqcho/) is a Rhodes Scholar and a top contributor to UK AI Security Institute's Inspect Evals. He has published papers in ICML, EMNLP, ACL, ACM EC and his research has been featured in MIT Technology Review. Previously, he spent time at AWS Bedrock, MATS, and Harvard where he completed his BA and MA with a highest honors thesis on AI and democracy.

If you build robots or AI models, reach out! We'd love to put them to the test. Learn more at [robocurve.org](http://robocurve.org).

launches.body:
We're [Caleb](https://www.linkedin.com/in/caleb-horan) and [Janak](https://www.linkedin.com/in/janak-panthi), PhD roboticists from UT Austin. We've spent a combined 15 years in nuclear, 10 of which deploying autonomous robots at Los Alamos National Lab, and we're building Salem Robotics.\
**TLDR:** Our software turns robots into independent survey and inspection workers at your facility.

[Launch Video](https://youtu.be/7xObOE6knZM)

## **Life and death pain worth $Millions/year**

At every nuclear facility, highly trained radiation-protection teams spend hours each day walking the site, filling out hand-drawn maps, and searching for something life-threatening: radiation. IN THE BEST CASE they find nothing, and still have to return to their posts to transcribe the data into a computer before doing the actual high-value work they were assigned. These surveys are time-consuming, dangerous, expensive, and prone to data inconsistencies that carry direct regulatory consequences.

The same pain exists well beyond nuclear. Whether it's gas-leak inspection or ammonia surveys, similar workflows run across oil, gas, chemical, biological, space, and other hazardous facilities.

## **What we do**

An operator defines the work from a simple dashboard; the robot then navigates the site, handles instruments, opens doors, turns valves, collects measurements, and generates structured, auditable, compliance-ready reports. We're hardware-agnostic, so plants run our software on robots they already own, many of which sit in a closet today as "$200k paperweights, " or we can provide the right robot for the job. Our stack is designed for safety-critical infrastructure and comes with theoretical safety guarantees, exactly what regulators and plant leadership require. Our core manipulation framework was not possible before and is based on **breakthrough founder research** published and presented at the most prestigious IEEE journals and conferences in the world. 

We're already in active contract-scoping conversations across the nuclear industry and oil & gas.

**Our asks**

* Intros to operations or innovation leaders in nuclear or similar hazardous sites (oil, gas, chem, bio, space).
* Advice from founders who've sold into safety-critical industrial environments.
* Sites where routine surveys are frequent, hard to staff, or particularly painful? We'd love to hear about them.

Comments, Emails, and DMs welcome. \

launches.tagline: Floating Nuclear Powered Data Centers At Sea
launches.body:
\*\*We're building floating data centers on barges powered by nuclear ships at sea.\*\*

<https://www.youtube.com/embed/unRTV4ZJXts?si=B5E5Z1xGe_NA7FLx>

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107426&key=user_uploads/697566/5530961e-115c-4010-b749-b4de1a939afa)


\
**TL;DR:** We move data center campuses offshore, away from communities, onto standardized barges we build on a single manufacturing line. That gets us near-free cooling, no interconnection queue, no local opposition, and 2x faster deployment. First gas-powered pilot ready by 2028.

Why now: AI has created unprecedented demand for compute and power that cannot be satisfied onshore.

* Grid interconnection timelines are **approaching a decade**.
* Data centers drive up the local cost of electricity, rent and land, and make water scarce. Community opposition rising from those reasons has **killed more than half of planned projects** since 2025.

What we're building: standardized, plug-and-play data center barges, built on one manufacturing line and towed to site. Moving offshore gives us:

* **No interconnection queue and no community impact** because our system operates standalone.
* More **scalable architecture** that offers **faster deployment** and tighter-controlled deliverability due to centralized construction and repeated site licensing
* **Lower energy cost** due to **less capacity overbuild** than onshore behind-the-meter and **cheaper financing** for repeatable manufacturing compared to on-site construction (financing = \~2/3 of the lifetime cost of a nuclear project)
* Virtually **free cooling** from seawater.

Traction: We already have early partnerships in place across the two hardest parts of this build:

* **Offshore design & construction:** working with established offshore barge designer/builders.
* **Nuclear power:** partnerships with multiple SMR vendors.

Why us: We're a two-founder team out of MIT with the exact mix this needs.

* [@Emile Germonpre](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/3640819) has a PhD in nuclear engineering.
* [@Dimitris Koutentakis](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/697566) has a BS/MEng in EECS, an MS in Mechanical Engineering, and an MBA, all from MIT, with deep connections to the Greek shipping industry.

**Our ask:** We're looking for intros to decision-makers in compute infrastructure or data center development we can sell to, VPs of Data Center Construction, Directors of Infrastructure, and hyperscaler / neocloud teams. If that's you or someone you know, reach out at [dimitris@atomarine.co](mailto:dimitris@atomarine.co) & [emile@atomarine.co](mailto:emile@atomarine.co).

name: Hemlock
long_description:
Every serious robotics lab is bottlenecked on the same thing: demonstration data. The field has converged on egocentric video and hand pose as the substrate, and both are now cheap to collect at scale. What neither of them contains is force. A video of someone picking up an egg and a video of someone picking up a rock are nearly identical in pixel space and nearly identical in joint angles. They differ almost entirely in a quantity nobody is recording. Policies trained without it learn geometry and inherit no sense of touch.

Hemlock closes that gap at the source. Our device, the Bracelet, is a wrist-worn surface EMG band that reads the electrical activity of the forearm muscles that actually drive the hand, which means it recovers contraction force directly rather than inferring it from motion. This distinction is the whole thesis: force cannot be reconstructed downstream of kinematics, because a hand squeezing hard isometrically and a hand resting can occupy the identical pose. Muscle signal is the only non-invasive channel that separates them.
one_liner: Force-sensing wristband for training robotic AI

launches.title: Dreamscale Labs: Running robot brains in the cloud
launches.tagline: The fastest cloud inference platform for robotics.
launches.body:
**TL;DR: We're 40-50% faster than existing cloud providers in serving frontier robot AI models, e.g. DreamZero, MolmoAct2.**

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jVqvJFBRcd0>

\[1x speed, autonomous\]

DSL is building the fastest cloud inference platform for robotics. We let you deploy physical AI without needing expensive local GPUs.

Robot foundation models are growing more and more computationally expensive. The latest frontier of robotics no longer fits feasibly on local GPUs. Compute costs keep soaring amidst a global LPDDR shortage; NVIDIA just doubled the prices of Jetsons in July.

**We're taking a contrarian bet that the future is moving inference _off the robot_ and _into the cloud._**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=115448&key=user_uploads/3499827/4ca20fc9-00a8-4043-bc43-d51b8b5d0cbf)

How do we do this? We work across the full stack of robot inference to push latency down:

* Model-level architectural adjustments for faster inference
* Kernel-level optimizations to maximally leverage server-grade GPUs
* Network-level optimizations for fast and reliable transport over the cloud
* Region-specific compute allocation to ensure the shortest physical distance between the servers and our customers' robots

These optimizations enable us to be **8% faster** than NVIDIA's implementation **at half the GPU count** (320ms vs 350ms, for DreamZero 14B).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=115448&key=user_uploads/3499827/69393040-ca17-41cd-a1fb-cd5d70176921)

Furthermore, something we noticed for robotics companies with fast R&D cycles was that their GPUs had long idle periods with concentrated bursts of inference traffic. We're one of the first companies in the world to offer on-demand pricing for physical AI inference, giving users more flexibility with the cost.

We're already working closely with a range of early partners across deployment, research and evaluation. In full FDE spirit, we collaborate with our customers to custom-fit inference stacks that address their unique deployment challenges. We help you get your robot AI to deployment faster.

Our mission is to democratize access to frontier physical intelligence, and we believe cloud is the way forward. You can read our thesis here:

•⁠ ⁠<http://dreamscalelabs.com/blog/why>

\
**Our ask:** Reach out at [founders@dreamscalelabs.com](mailto:founders@dreamscalelabs.com) !
